de-ahrweiler-garkammer.name: Ahrweilerer Gärkammer
de-ahrweiler-garkammer.summary: The Gärkammer is a tiny walled slope of about 0.7 ha at Walporzheim, the monopole of J. J. Adeneuer, giving dense, smoky Pinot Noir.
de-ahrweiler-garkammer.terroir: Slate and greywacke in a sheltered hollow. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Walporzheim/Ahrtal and the Grosslage Klosterberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Ahrweiler include Rosenthal, Silberberg and Kräuterberg.

de-ahrweiler-krauterberg.name: Ahrweilerer Kräuterberg
de-ahrweiler-krauterberg.summary: The Kräuterberg ('herb hill') at Walporzheim is the Ahr's most legendary slope, a narrow amphitheatre of terraces held up by slate walls, so steep and hot that wild herbs grow between the vines. Its Pinot Noirs are dark, spicy and concentrated, with a cool slate finish. Meyer-Näkel and Jean Stodden have helped restore its terraces, several of which had been abandoned. The catastrophic flood of 14 July 2021 devastated the valley's villages and cellars; the steep vineyards themselves mostly survived.
de-ahrweiler-krauterberg.terroir: About 5 ha of Devonian slate and greywacke terraces facing south and south-west; the walls and rock store heat in a valley that is otherwise one of Germany's northernmost red-wine areas. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Walporzheim/Ahrtal and the Grosslage Klosterberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 5.1 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Ahrweiler include Rosenthal, Silberberg and Gärkammer.
de-ahrweiler-krauterberg.nerd_note: The legal label calls it Ahrweilerer Kräuterberg because Walporzheim belongs to Bad Neuenahr-Ahrweiler, but growers still use the historic name Walporzheimer Kräuterberg.

de-ahrweiler-rosenthal.name: Ahrweilerer Rosenthal
de-ahrweiler-rosenthal.summary: The Rosenthal is a sheltered, south-facing Ahrweiler site where loess and loam over slate give rounder, fleshier Pinot Noir than the bare slopes upstream. J. J. Adeneuer and Meyer-Näkel bottle it.
de-ahrweiler-rosenthal.terroir: About 21 ha of loess and loam over slate and greywacke. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Walporzheim/Ahrtal and the Grosslage Klosterberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 21 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Ahrweiler include Silberberg, Gärkammer and Kräuterberg.

de-ahrweiler-silberberg.name: Ahrweilerer Silberberg
de-ahrweiler-silberberg.summary: A steep Ahrweiler site of about 14 ha on slate, giving firm, fine Pinot Noir from Meyer-Näkel and others.
de-ahrweiler-silberberg.terroir: Slate and greywacke with quartzite. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Walporzheim/Ahrtal and the Grosslage Klosterberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 14 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Ahrweiler include Rosenthal, Gärkammer and Kräuterberg.

de-altenahr-eck.name: Altenahrer Eck
de-altenahr-eck.summary: The Eck at Altenahr is the uppermost great site of the Ahr, a steep, rocky slope at a bend of the river where Deutzerhof and Jean Stodden make taut, mineral Pinot Noir.
de-altenahr-eck.terroir: About 10 ha of slate and greywacke, very steep, south facing. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Walporzheim/Ahrtal and the Grosslage Klosterberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 9.6 ha are registered under vine.

de-arzheim-kalmit.name: Kalmit
de-arzheim-kalmit.summary: The Kalmit, shared by Arzheim and Ilbesheim, is a limestone hill where Kranz makes one of the most admired Rieslings of the southern Pfalz.
de-arzheim-kalmit.terroir: About 94 ha of shell limestone and marl on south-facing slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Südl. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Herrlich (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 93.8 ha are registered under vine.

de-ayl-herrenberger.name: Ayler Herrenberger
de-ayl-herrenberger.summary: A small Ayl site long associated with the Bischöfliches Konvikt of Trier, the Herrenberger gives lean, floral Saar Riesling.
de-ayl-herrenberger.terroir: Steep slate on a south-facing spur. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Ayl include Kupp.

de-ayl-kupp.name: Kupp
de-ayl-kupp.summary: The Ayler Kupp is a broad, steep slope of slate above Ayl, about 50 ha in its modern form. Peter Lauer turned it into one of the Saar's most studied sites by bottling historic parcels separately under cask numbers: Kern, Stirn, Unterstenberg and Schonfels each show a different face, from delicate and floral to dense and smoky. The Bischöfliche Weingüter and several smaller growers also work here. The best wines combine Saar acidity with a creamy texture that comes from old vines and long lees ageing.
de-ayl-kupp.terroir: Grey and blue Devonian slate with patches of weathered rock and loam, south to south-east facing, roughly 150 to 300 m; the side valley of the Ayl brook brings cool night air. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 53.3 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Ayl include Herrenberger.
de-ayl-kupp.nerd_note: Lauer's parcel names come from the old cadastre, many of them erased when the 1971 wine law merged small sites into larger Einzellagen.

de-bacharach-hahn.name: Bacharacher Hahn
de-bacharach-hahn.summary: The Hahn is a steep, south-facing slope of slate just upstream of Bacharach, the monopole of Toni Jost. Its Rieslings are taut and racy, with a smoky slate finish, and Jost also makes sweet wines of great purity here. In the Middle Ages Bacharach was the shipping port for Rhine wine, which was sold far and wide as 'Bacharacher'; the town walls and towers still run along the vineyard edge.
de-bacharach-hahn.terroir: About 5 ha of grey Devonian slate rising directly from the Rhine. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Loreley and the Grosslage Schloß Stahleck (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bacharach include Wolfshöhle, Posten and St. Jost.

de-bacharach-posten.name: Bacharacher Posten
de-bacharach-posten.summary: The Posten lies right behind the town walls of Bacharach, a steep slope of slate where Ratzenberger and Bastian make fine, aromatic Riesling.
de-bacharach-posten.terroir: About 5 ha of slate on a south-east-facing slope above the old town. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Loreley and the Grosslage Schloß Stahleck (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 4.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bacharach include Wolfshöhle, Hahn and St. Jost.

de-bacharach-st-jost.name: St. Jost
de-bacharach-st-jost.summary: St. Jost in the Steeg side valley above Bacharach is a steep slate site named after a chapel of St. Jodocus. Ratzenberger's Rieslings and sparkling wines from here are taut and elegant.
de-bacharach-st-jost.terroir: About 7 ha of slate in a cooler side valley. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Loreley and the Grosslage Schloß Stahleck (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 6.7 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bacharach include Wolfshöhle, Hahn and Posten.

de-bacharach-wolfshohle.name: Bacharacher Wolfshöhle
de-bacharach-wolfshohle.summary: A steep Bacharach site of about 22 ha whose slate gives cool, firm Riesling, notably from Ratzenberger.
de-bacharach-wolfshohle.terroir: Slate on the slopes around the Steeg valley. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Loreley and the Grosslage Schloß Stahleck (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 21.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bacharach include Hahn, Posten and St. Jost.

de-bad-durkheim-michelsberg.name: Michelsberg
de-bad-durkheim-michelsberg.summary: The Michelsberg rises above Bad Dürkheim next to the ruins of a chapel of St. Michael, site of the town's famous wine fair (the Wurstmarkt) since the Middle Ages. It gives ripe, aromatic Riesling.
de-bad-durkheim-michelsberg.terroir: About 8 ha of limestone and sandstone. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Hochmess (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 7.7 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bad Dürkheim include Spielberg.

de-bad-durkheim-spielberg.name: Dürkheimer Spielberg
de-bad-durkheim-spielberg.summary: A Bad Dürkheim site of about 14 ha on limestone, giving firm Riesling and fine Pinot Noir from Rings and Karl Schaefer.
de-bad-durkheim-spielberg.terroir: Limestone and loam. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Hochmess (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 14.1 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bad Dürkheim include Michelsberg.

de-bad-kreuznach-bruckes.name: Kreuznacher Brückes
de-bad-kreuznach-bruckes.summary: A Bad Kreuznach site of about 6.4 ha with deep loess and sandstone soils, giving rich, aromatic Riesling for town estates.
de-bad-kreuznach-bruckes.terroir: Loess and sandstone near the centre of Bad Kreuznach. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Kronenberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 6.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bad Kreuznach include Kahlenberg and Krötenpfuhl.

de-bad-kreuznach-kahlenberg.name: Kreuznacher Kahlenberg
de-bad-kreuznach-kahlenberg.summary: The Kahlenberg is a Bad Kreuznach slope of about 17 ha on gravel, loam and sandstone, giving full, fruity Riesling, notably from Dönnhoff and Kreuznach estates.
de-bad-kreuznach-kahlenberg.terroir: Weathered sandstone, gravel and loam on south-facing slopes on the edge of the spa town. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Kronenberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 16.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bad Kreuznach include Brückes and Krötenpfuhl.

de-bad-kreuznach-krotenpfuhl.name: Kreuznacher Krötenpfuhl
de-bad-kreuznach-krotenpfuhl.summary: The Krötenpfuhl ('toad pond') in Bad Kreuznach gives a creamy, ripe Riesling on deep gravel and loam, a very different face of the Nahe from the volcanic sites upstream. Dönnhoff's Krötenpfuhl is a reference.
de-bad-kreuznach-krotenpfuhl.terroir: About 6.4 ha of gravel, loess and clay on a gentle slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Kronenberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 6.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bad Kreuznach include Kahlenberg and Brückes.

de-bad-neuenahr-sonnenberg.name: Neuenahrer Sonnenberg
de-bad-neuenahr-sonnenberg.summary: A Bad Neuenahr site of about 24 ha with loess and slate, giving supple Pinot Noir, notably from J. J. Adeneuer and Jean Stodden.
de-bad-neuenahr-sonnenberg.terroir: Loess and loam over slate. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Walporzheim/Ahrtal and the Grosslage Klosterberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 23.7 ha are registered under vine.

de-bechtheim-geyersberg.name: Bechtheimer Geyersberg
de-bechtheim-geyersberg.summary: A Bechtheim site of about 79 ha on limestone and loess, giving full, ripe Riesling and Pinot.
de-bechtheim-geyersberg.terroir: Limestone, loess and marl. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Wonnegau and the Grosslage Pilgerpfad (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 79.1 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bechtheim include Hasensprung.

de-bechtheim-hasensprung.name: Bechtheimer Hasensprung
de-bechtheim-hasensprung.summary: A large Bechtheim site of about 174 ha on loess and limestone, giving ripe white and red wines.
de-bechtheim-hasensprung.terroir: Loess over limestone. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Wonnegau and the Grosslage Pilgerpfad (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 173.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bechtheim include Geyersberg.

de-bernkastel-alte-badstube-am-doctorber.name: Bernkasteler Alte Badstube am Doctorberg
de-bernkastel-alte-badstube-am-doctorber.summary: A tiny slope next to the Doctor, the Alte Badstube am Doctorberg gives very similar, rich and smoky Riesling at a fraction of the price.
de-bernkastel-alte-badstube-am-doctorber.terroir: About 1.6 ha of slate on the same steep hillside as the Doctor. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Münzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 1.6 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bernkastel include Badstube, Graben, Lay and Doctor.

de-bernkastel-badstube.name: Bernkasteler Badstube
de-bernkastel-badstube.summary: Badstube is a collective Einzellage name for several steep Bernkastel slopes around the Doctor, about 26 ha, giving fruity, accessible Riesling.
de-bernkastel-badstube.terroir: Slate slopes facing south and south-west above the town. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Münzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 25.6 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bernkastel include Graben, Lay, Alte Badstube am Doctorberg and Doctor.

de-bernkastel-doctor.name: Bernkasteler Doctor
de-bernkastel-doctor.summary: The Doctor is Germany's most famous vineyard, a tiny, very steep slope rising directly behind the rooftops of Bernkastel. Legend says its wine cured the fourteenth-century Archbishop Boemund II of Trier of a fever. In 1900 a small parcel is said to have sold for 100 gold marks per vine, a record price for vineyard land. Wwe. Dr. H. Thanisch (both branches), Wegeler and Lauerburg share it, and the wines are rich, smoky and long, with a distinctive mineral warmth.
de-bernkastel-doctor.terroir: About 3.3 ha of weathered grey slate on a south-south-west slope of up to 60 percent, sheltered by the town and the Kueser Plateau; it ripens early and gets very warm. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Münzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 3.3 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bernkastel include Badstube, Graben, Lay and Alte Badstube am Doctorberg.
de-bernkastel-doctor.nerd_note: When the 1971 wine law tried to enlarge the Doctor to take in neighbouring slopes, the owners went to court; the boundary finally settled at about 3.3 ha, still a fraction of its neighbours.

de-bernkastel-graben.name: Bernkasteler Graben
de-bernkastel-graben.summary: A steep Bernkastel slope of about 10 ha next to the Doctor, giving spicy, concentrated Riesling.
de-bernkastel-graben.terroir: Slate on a south-facing slope above the town. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Münzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 10.3 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bernkastel include Badstube, Lay, Alte Badstube am Doctorberg and Doctor.

de-bernkastel-lay.name: Bernkasteler Lay
de-bernkastel-lay.summary: The Lay is a steep slope just downstream of the Doctor, overlooking the bridge at Bernkastel. Its Rieslings are fine and elegant, with a cooler profile than its famous neighbour.
de-bernkastel-lay.terroir: About 9.5 ha of grey slate ('Lay' means slate rock) facing south-west. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Münzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 9.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bernkastel include Badstube, Graben, Alte Badstube am Doctorberg and Doctor.

de-bingerbrueck-abtei-rupertsberg.name: Abtei Rupertsberg
de-bingerbrueck-abtei-rupertsberg.summary: The Abtei Rupertsberg site at Bingerbrück recalls the convent Hildegard of Bingen founded on the Rupertsberg around 1150 after leaving the Disibodenberg. A few hectares of vines grow on the hill where the Nahe meets the Rhine.
de-bingerbrueck-abtei-rupertsberg.terroir: Quartzite and slate on slopes above the confluence. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Schlosskapelle (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 4.7 ha are registered under vine.

de-birkweiler-kastanienbusch.name: Birkweilerer Kastanienbusch
de-birkweiler-kastanienbusch.summary: The Kastanienbusch ('chestnut grove') at Birkweiler is the great site of the southern Pfalz, rising to over 300 m at the edge of the Palatinate Forest. Its unusual red soils from Rotliegend, plus granite and slate, give Rieslings of spice, power and length; the steep 'Köppel' parcel is the core. Dr. Wehrheim, Ökonomierat Rebholz, Siegrist and Gies-Düppel make the reference wines.
de-birkweiler-kastanienbusch.terroir: About 67 ha registered, with red Rotliegend sandstone, weathered granite and slate on steep, south-east-facing slopes; chestnut woods surround the vines and cool nights keep acidity bright. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Südl. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Königsgarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 67.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Birkweiler include Mandelberg.
de-birkweiler-kastanienbusch.nerd_note: Few places in Germany show such a jumble of rocks within one slope; growers bottle the Köppel separately because of its red stony soil.

de-birkweiler-mandelberg.name: Birkweilerer Mandelberg
de-birkweiler-mandelberg.summary: The Mandelberg at Birkweiler is a limestone site famous for Pinot Blanc and Pinot Gris, especially Dr. Wehrheim's Weissburgunder Grosses Gewächs.
de-birkweiler-mandelberg.terroir: About 27 ha of limestone (Muschelkalk) and marl. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Südl. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Königsgarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 26.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Birkweiler include Kastanienbusch.

de-bockenau-felseneck.name: Bockenauer Felseneck
de-bockenau-felseneck.summary: The Felseneck is a very steep, rocky slope in the Ellerbach valley at Bockenau, a side valley north of the Nahe. Tim Fröhlich of Schäfer-Fröhlich turned this once-obscure site into one of Germany's most sought-after dry Rieslings: smoky, wild-yeast fermented, crystalline and intense.
de-bockenau-felseneck.terroir: About 10 ha of blue and grey Devonian slate on a steep south-facing slope, cooler and higher than the main Nahe valley. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Rosengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 10.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bockenau include Stromberg.
de-bockenau-felseneck.nerd_note: Bockenau had no reputation before Schäfer-Fröhlich; the Felseneck shows how much the German wine map has been redrawn by growers since 2000.

de-bockenau-stromberg.name: Bockenauer Stromberg
de-bockenau-stromberg.summary: A small Bockenau slope of slate where Schäfer-Fröhlich makes a cooler, tighter Grosses Gewächs than the Felseneck.
de-bockenau-stromberg.terroir: Grey slate on a steep, high slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Rosengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Bockenau include Felseneck.

de-bodenheim-burgweg.name: Burgweg
de-bodenheim-burgweg.summary: The Burgweg, shared by Bodenheim and Mainz-Laubenheim, is a home site of Kühling-Gillot, giving firm, mineral Riesling on limestone.
de-bodenheim-burgweg.terroir: About 41 ha of limestone, marl and loess. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nierstein and the Grosslage Sankt Alban (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 41.3 ha are registered under vine.

de-boppard-engelstein.name: Engelstein
de-boppard-engelstein.summary: A small section of the Bopparder Hamm shared with Spay, giving fine, fragrant Riesling.
de-boppard-engelstein.terroir: Slate on the downstream arm of the loop. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Loreley and the Grosslage Gedeonseck (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 3.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Boppard include Feuerlay, Mandelstein and Ohlenberg.

de-boppard-feuerlay.name: Bopparder Feuerlay
de-boppard-feuerlay.summary: The Feuerlay ('fire rock') is the best-known section of the Bopparder Hamm, the great loop of the Rhine at Boppard where the river turns through 180 degrees and the slope faces full south. Matthias Müller's Rieslings from here are fine, spicy and long, with a cool slate finish.
de-boppard-feuerlay.terroir: About 17 ha of Devonian slate on steep south-facing slopes at the apex of the bend; the wide river reflects light, and the deep gorge shelters the vines from cold winds. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Loreley and the Grosslage Gedeonseck (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 16.7 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Boppard include Engelstein, Mandelstein and Ohlenberg.
de-boppard-feuerlay.nerd_note: The Bopparder Hamm is divided into several Einzellagen (Feuerlay, Mandelstein, Ohlenberg, Engelstein, Fässerlay, Elfenlay, Weingrube); the whole loop sits inside the Upper Middle Rhine Valley UNESCO World Heritage Site.

de-boppard-mandelstein.name: Bopparder Mandelstein
de-boppard-mandelstein.summary: A steep section of the Bopparder Hamm, about 11 ha, giving ripe, mineral Riesling from Matthias Müller and others.
de-boppard-mandelstein.terroir: Slate, south-facing. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Loreley and the Grosslage Gedeonseck (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 10.7 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Boppard include Feuerlay, Engelstein and Ohlenberg.

de-boppard-ohlenberg.name: Bopparder Ohlenberg
de-boppard-ohlenberg.summary: A section of the Bopparder Hamm of about 8 ha, giving firm, slatey Riesling.
de-boppard-ohlenberg.terroir: Devonian slate on a steep slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Loreley and the Grosslage Gedeonseck (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 8.1 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Boppard include Feuerlay, Engelstein and Mandelstein.

de-brauneberg-juffer.name: Juffer
de-brauneberg-juffer.summary: The Juffer is the broad, steep wall of slate opposite Brauneberg, the village that was called Dusemond (from mons dulcis, 'sweet hill') until 1925. Its Rieslings are rich, ripe and spicy, with a juicy core and a long slate finish. Fritz Haag, Schloss Lieser, Max Ferd. Richter, Paulinshof and Willi Haag are the key growers.
de-brauneberg-juffer.terroir: Grey Devonian slate with weathered loam on a south-south-east-facing slope rising from the river; the Mosel is wide here and reflects a lot of light. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Kurfürstlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 31.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Brauneberg include Juffer Sonnenuhr and Kammer.
de-brauneberg-juffer.nerd_note: Local lore says the name comes from 'Jungfer' (young lady), after unmarried daughters of a local official who owned parcels here.

de-brauneberg-juffer-sonnenuhr.name: Brauneberger Juffer Sonnenuhr
de-brauneberg-juffer-sonnenuhr.summary: The Juffer-Sonnenuhr is the steep core of the Brauneberger Juffer, marked by a sundial. In the hands of Fritz Haag (and of Schloss Lieser, run by Thomas Haag) it yields some of the most complete Rieslings of the Mosel: creamy, concentrated, layered with peach, spice and slate, and capable of ageing for decades. Nineteenth-century price lists already placed Brauneberg among the first villages of the Mosel.
de-brauneberg-juffer-sonnenuhr.terroir: About 10.6 ha of grey slate on the steepest, best-exposed part of the slope, facing south directly over the river. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Kurfürstlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 10.6 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Brauneberg include Juffer and Kammer.
de-brauneberg-juffer-sonnenuhr.nerd_note: Fritz Haag's Auslese gold capsules and long-gold capsules from the Juffer-Sonnenuhr are among the most collected sweet Rieslings in the world.

de-brauneberg-kammer.name: Brauneberger Kammer
de-brauneberg-kammer.summary: A small, walled Brauneberg site long associated with Weingut Paulinshof, giving ripe, fine-textured Riesling.
de-brauneberg-kammer.terroir: Slate in a sheltered position next to the Juffer. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Kurfürstlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Brauneberg include Juffer and Juffer Sonnenuhr.

de-bremm-calmont.name: Calmont
de-bremm-calmont.summary: The Calmont, between Bremm and Ediger-Eller, is often called the steepest vineyard in Europe, with gradients of up to 65 degrees on a cliff of slate and quartzite above a tight loop of the Mosel. Much of it was abandoned in the late twentieth century; growers such as Weingut Franzen in Bremm have brought terraces back into production. The wines are concentrated, ripe and spicy, with a cool mineral line from the rock. A via ferrata (Calmont Klettersteig) crosses the slope.
de-bremm-calmont.terroir: About 18 ha under vine on a south-facing wall of Devonian slate and quartzite; the rock and the river make it one of the warmest sites of the lower Mosel despite its northerly position. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Burg Cochem and the Grosslage Grafschaft (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 18.2 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bremm include Frauenberg.
de-bremm-calmont.nerd_note: Archaeologists have found the remains of a Gallo-Roman temple on the summit; the name is often derived from Latin calidus mons, 'warm mountain'.

de-bremm-frauenberg.name: Frauenberg
de-bremm-frauenberg.summary: A steep site shared by Bremm and Neef, opposite the Calmont, named after the ruined Stuben convent below it. It gives ripe, slatey Riesling.
de-bremm-frauenberg.terroir: About 14.5 ha of steep slate. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Burg Cochem and the Grosslage Grafschaft (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 14.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bremm include Calmont.

de-budesheim-scharlachberg.name: Büdesheimer Scharlachberg
de-budesheim-scharlachberg.summary: The Scharlachberg ('scarlet hill') at Bingen-Büdesheim owes its name to red quartzite and slate soils. It is the best-known site of Bingen, giving spicy, mineral Riesling.
de-budesheim-scharlachberg.terroir: About 26 ha of quartzite and red slate on steep south-facing slopes above the Nahe and Rhine, geologically close to the Rheingau's Rüdesheimer Berg. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bingen and the Grosslage St. Rochuskapelle (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 25.6 ha are registered under vine.

de-burrweiler-schawer.name: Burrweilerer Schäwer
de-burrweiler-schawer.summary: The Schäwer at Burrweiler is the only slate site of the Pfalz, a small outcrop of the same kind of rock as the Mosel. Herbert Messmer's Rieslings from it are cool, fine and slatey.
de-burrweiler-schawer.terroir: About 23 ha registered, with Devonian slate on the slopes of the Haardt. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Südl. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Bischofskreuz (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 23.2 ha are registered under vine.
de-burrweiler-schawer.nerd_note: The name comes from the dialect word for slate ('Schiefer').

de-cochem-pinnerkreuzberg.name: Cochemer Pinnerkreuzberg
de-cochem-pinnerkreuzberg.summary: A steep site behind Cochem named after a wayside cross, giving cool, firm Riesling.
de-cochem-pinnerkreuzberg.terroir: Slate above the town, facing south. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Burg Cochem and the Grosslage Goldbäumchen (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages).

de-dalsheim-burgel.name: Dalsheimer Bürgel
de-dalsheim-burgel.summary: A large Dalsheim site of about 84 ha on limestone where Keller grows outstanding Pinot Noir and Silvaner as well as Riesling.
de-dalsheim-burgel.terroir: Limestone and marl with some loess. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Wonnegau and the Grosslage Burg Rodenstein (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 83.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Dalsheim include Hubacker.

de-dalsheim-hubacker.name: Dalsheimer Hubacker
de-dalsheim-hubacker.summary: The Hubacker is the founding site of Weingut Keller in Flörsheim-Dalsheim, a gentle limestone slope that helped make Klaus and Klaus Peter Keller famous. Its dry Riesling is concentrated, mineral and slow to open. The Keller family has farmed in Flörsheim-Dalsheim since 1789. Their cult Riesling G-Max is sold without a site name, and the estate keeps its exact source secret.
de-dalsheim-hubacker.terroir: About 23 ha of limestone with thin clay marl, facing south-east. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Wonnegau and the Grosslage Burg Rodenstein (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 22.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Dalsheim include Bürgel.

de-deidesheim-grainhubel.name: Deidesheimer Grainhübel
de-deidesheim-grainhubel.summary: A Deidesheim site of about 5 ha giving spicy, elegant Riesling, from Bassermann-Jordan and von Winning among others.
de-deidesheim-grainhubel.terroir: Sandstone, loam and limestone. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 5.3 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Deidesheim include Paradiesgarten, Kieselberg, Leinhöhle and Langenmorgen.

de-deidesheim-hohenmorgen.name: Deidesheimer Hohenmorgen
de-deidesheim-hohenmorgen.summary: The Hohenmorgen is a tiny, slightly elevated site of about 2.8 ha in Deidesheim, giving a dense, deep Riesling with smoky spice. Bassermann-Jordan and Bürklin-Wolf are the main owners.
de-deidesheim-hohenmorgen.terroir: Sandstone and loam with some limestone, east facing. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 2.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Deidesheim include Paradiesgarten, Kieselberg, Leinhöhle and Grainhübel.

de-deidesheim-kalkofen.name: Deidesheimer Kalkofen
de-deidesheim-kalkofen.summary: The Kalkofen ('lime kiln') in Deidesheim is named after the limestone that was burned here; it gives full, firm Riesling with a chalky grip.
de-deidesheim-kalkofen.terroir: About 5 ha of limestone and loam. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 4.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Deidesheim include Paradiesgarten, Kieselberg, Leinhöhle and Grainhübel.

de-deidesheim-kieselberg.name: Deidesheimer Kieselberg
de-deidesheim-kieselberg.summary: A Deidesheim site of about 16 ha with pebbly soils, giving fresh, elegant Riesling.
de-deidesheim-kieselberg.terroir: Sand, gravel and pebbles ('Kiesel'). In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 15.7 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Deidesheim include Paradiesgarten, Leinhöhle, Grainhübel and Langenmorgen.

de-deidesheim-langenmorgen.name: Deidesheimer Langenmorgen
de-deidesheim-langenmorgen.summary: The Langenmorgen is a long, narrow Deidesheim site of about 10 ha where von Winning makes one of its most celebrated Grosse Gewächse: aromatic, oak-framed and long.
de-deidesheim-langenmorgen.terroir: Sandy loam over sandstone on a gentle slope below the Haardt forest. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 9.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Deidesheim include Paradiesgarten, Kieselberg, Leinhöhle and Grainhübel.

de-deidesheim-leinhohle.name: Deidesheimer Leinhöhle
de-deidesheim-leinhohle.summary: A Deidesheim site of about 18 ha, giving juicy, fragrant Riesling from Bassermann-Jordan, von Winning and others.
de-deidesheim-leinhohle.terroir: Sandy loam and sandstone rubble. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 17.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Deidesheim include Paradiesgarten, Kieselberg, Grainhübel and Langenmorgen.

de-deidesheim-paradiesgarten.name: Deidesheimer Paradiesgarten
de-deidesheim-paradiesgarten.summary: A Deidesheim site of about 30 ha at the forest edge, giving fresh Riesling and Pinot.
de-deidesheim-paradiesgarten.terroir: Sandstone and loam, higher and cooler. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 30.2 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Deidesheim include Kieselberg, Leinhöhle, Grainhübel and Langenmorgen.

de-dernau-hardtberg.name: Dernauer Hardtberg
de-dernau-hardtberg.summary: A Dernau site of about 24 ha on slate, giving cool, finely spiced Pinot Noir, for Meyer-Näkel and Kreuzberg.
de-dernau-hardtberg.terroir: Slate and greywacke, steep and terraced in parts. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Walporzheim/Ahrtal and the Grosslage Klosterberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 24 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Dernau include Pfarrwingert.

de-dernau-pfarrwingert.name: Dernauer Pfarrwingert
de-dernau-pfarrwingert.summary: The Pfarrwingert ('parish vineyard') at Dernau is a steep slope of slate whose Pinot Noirs, especially from Meyer-Näkel, are fine-boned, perfumed and long.
de-dernau-pfarrwingert.terroir: About 9 ha of Devonian slate and greywacke on a south-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Walporzheim/Ahrtal and the Grosslage Klosterberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 8.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Dernau include Hardtberg.

de-dhron-goldtropfchen.name: Goldtröpfchen
de-dhron-goldtropfchen.summary: Piesport's Goldtröpfchen is one of the Mosel's most perfect natural amphitheatres, a south-facing bowl curving around the village that gives some of the most opulent, aromatic Rieslings of the valley: blackcurrant, peach, citrus and a hint of spice over a juicy slate core. Reinhold Haart, Julian Haart, Reichsgraf von Kesselstatt, Sankt Urbans-Hof and Grans-Fassian are the names to look for. The site's reputation was blurred for decades by the bulk wine 'Piesporter Michelsberg', a Grosslage that borrowed the village's fame.
de-dhron-goldtropfchen.terroir: Grey Devonian slate with a deeper, more fertile weathered layer on a steep south-facing bowl; the Mosel bends around it so that heat and light are reflected back onto the vines. The 2026 vineyard register lists about 64 ha under vine across Piesport, Niederemmel and Dhron. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Michelsberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 64.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Dhron include Hofberger, Roterd and Häs'chen.
de-dhron-goldtropfchen.nerd_note: Archaeologists found a Roman wine press house in Piesport in 1985, one of the largest north of the Alps, a sign that this bowl has been prized for at least 1,600 years.

de-dhron-has-chen.name: Dhroner Häs'chen
de-dhron-has-chen.summary: A tiny, steep parcel in Dhron that A.J. Adam bottles separately, giving fine, floral Riesling.
de-dhron-has-chen.terroir: Slate on a sheltered slope in the Dhron valley. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Michelsberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Dhron include Hofberger, Roterd and Goldtröpfchen.

de-dhron-hofberger.name: Hofberger
de-dhron-hofberger.summary: The Hofberger rises above the Dhron valley where the little river joins the Mosel. Andreas Adam of A.J. Adam has made it famous again with taut, smoky Rieslings, including from very old vines. Its cooler side-valley exposure gives a precise, almost Saar-like acidity.
de-dhron-hofberger.terroir: Grey slate on steep south and south-west slopes in the mouth of the Dhron valley, cooled by air draining down the side valley; about 73 ha are registered under vine. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Michelsberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 73.1 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Dhron include Roterd, Goldtröpfchen and Häs'chen.
de-dhron-hofberger.nerd_note: A 'Dhronhofberger' features in the VDP Mosel's early auction history, a sign of its standing a century ago.

de-dhron-roterd.name: Dhroner Roterd
de-dhron-roterd.summary: The Roterd ('red earth') above Dhron owes its name to red, iron-rich weathered slate. It gives warm, aromatic Riesling.
de-dhron-roterd.terroir: Red slate soils on a south-facing slope of the Dhron valley. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Michelsberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 44.2 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Dhron include Hofberger, Goldtröpfchen and Häs'chen.

de-dienheim-kreuz.name: Kreuz
de-dienheim-kreuz.summary: The Kreuz, shared by Dienheim and Oppenheim, is a broad slope of loess and limestone giving ripe, round white wines.
de-dienheim-kreuz.terroir: About 49 ha of loess over limestone. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nierstein and the Grosslage Güldenmorgen (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 48.9 ha are registered under vine.

de-dorsheim-burgberg.name: Dorsheimer Burgberg
de-dorsheim-burgberg.summary: A small Dorsheim site of about 3.8 ha below a castle, giving concentrated, mineral Riesling from Schlossgut Diel.
de-dorsheim-burgberg.terroir: Stony quartzite and slate on a steep slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Schlosskapelle (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 3.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Dorsheim include Goldloch and Pittermännchen.

de-dorsheim-goldloch.name: Dorsheimer Goldloch
de-dorsheim-goldloch.summary: The Goldloch ('gold hole') at Dorsheim is one of the three great sites of Schlossgut Diel, a warm amphitheatre of stony soils giving opulent, spicy Riesling, both dry and fruity-sweet.
de-dorsheim-goldloch.terroir: About 10 ha of gravelly loam over quartzite and slate in a sheltered bowl. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Schlosskapelle (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 10.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Dorsheim include Burgberg and Pittermännchen.

de-dorsheim-pittermannchen.name: Dorsheimer Pittermännchen
de-dorsheim-pittermannchen.summary: The Pittermännchen is a small, steep Dorsheim slope of slate and quartzite where Schlossgut Diel makes a fine, cool, citrus-driven Riesling. The odd name is said to recall a small silver coin, the Pittermännchen, once paid for the land.
de-dorsheim-pittermannchen.terroir: About 7.4 ha of slate and quartzite on a steep slope facing south-west. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Schlosskapelle (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 7.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Dorsheim include Burgberg and Goldloch.

de-eitelsbach-karthauserhofberg.name: Eitelsbacher Karthäuserhofberg
de-eitelsbach-karthauserhofberg.summary: The Karthäuserhofberg is the monopole of the Karthäuserhof in Eitelsbach, an estate that belonged to the Carthusians of Trier from 1335 until Napoleon's secularisation, when it was auctioned in 1811 to Valentin Leonardy, whose descendants, the Rautenstrauch and Tyrell families, ran it for two centuries. The wines are among the Ruwer's most aristocratic: fine-boned, smoky and very long, with acidity that carries them for decades. The estate is known for its neck-only label, a nineteenth-century design that leaves the bottle body bare.
de-eitelsbach-karthauserhofberg.terroir: About 19 ha of grey and red Devonian slate on a south-facing slope rising behind the manor, cool and windy in the narrow Ruwer valley. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Ruwer and belongs to no Grosslage.
de-eitelsbach-karthauserhofberg.nerd_note: Every wine the estate makes comes from this one slope, so the Karthäuserhofberg is as much a brand as a vineyard.

de-enkirch-batterieberg.name: Enkircher Batterieberg
de-enkirch-batterieberg.summary: The Batterieberg is the monopole of Weingut Immich-Batterieberg in Enkirch. In the 1840s Carl August Immich blasted the slope out of rock with explosives, and the name recalls the 'battery' of charges. The wines are taut, smoky and long, mostly made in a dry or off-dry style.
de-enkirch-batterieberg.terroir: About 1 ha of bare blue slate on an extremely steep, south-facing terrace. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Schwarzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Enkirch include Steffensberg, Ellergrub and Zeppwingert.

de-enkirch-ellergrub.name: Enkircher Ellergrub
de-enkirch-ellergrub.summary: The Ellergrub is a very steep, hot amphitheatre in Enkirch that Weiser-Künstler and Immich-Batterieberg have made famous again. Its Riesling is intense, spicy and deep.
de-enkirch-ellergrub.terroir: About 6 ha of blue slate on a steep, south-facing bowl. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Schwarzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 5.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Enkirch include Steffensberg, Zeppwingert and Batterieberg.

de-enkirch-steffensberg.name: Enkircher Steffensberg
de-enkirch-steffensberg.summary: A long Enkirch slope of about 30 ha, giving elegant, fruity Riesling, for example from Weiser-Künstler.
de-enkirch-steffensberg.terroir: Slate on a south-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Schwarzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 30.3 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Enkirch include Ellergrub, Zeppwingert and Batterieberg.

de-enkirch-zeppwingert.name: Enkircher Zeppwingert
de-enkirch-zeppwingert.summary: A steep Enkirch site of about 9 ha giving precise, mineral Riesling, notably from Immich-Batterieberg.
de-enkirch-zeppwingert.terroir: Grey slate on a south-west-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Schwarzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 9.2 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Enkirch include Steffensberg, Ellergrub and Batterieberg.

de-erden-busslay.name: Erdener Busslay
de-erden-busslay.summary: A larger Erden site of about 59 ha downstream of the Treppchen, giving fruity, mineral Riesling, including from old vines.
de-erden-busslay.terroir: Slate on a south-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Schwarzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 59 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Erden include Treppchen and Prälat.

de-erden-pralat.name: Erdener Prälat
de-erden-pralat.summary: The Prälat is one of the Mosel's smallest great sites, about 1.5 ha squeezed between red cliffs and the river below Erden. It is the warmest spot of the Middle Mosel: the rock walls store heat, the river reflects light and the vines face full south. Dr. Loosen's Auslese and Grosses Gewächs from here are rich, exotic and endlessly long, with spice from the red soils. Mönchhof and Jos. Christoffel also own parcels.
de-erden-pralat.terroir: Red slate and weathered red sandstone in a narrow strip between a cliff and the water, with almost no frost and the earliest ripening of the area. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Schwarzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 1.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Erden include Busslay and Treppchen.
de-erden-pralat.nerd_note: Archaeologists excavated a Roman press house in Erden in the 1990s, below the Treppchen and Prälat, now partly reconstructed.

de-erden-treppchen.name: Erdener Treppchen
de-erden-treppchen.summary: The Treppchen ('little staircase') is named after the stone steps cut into the steep slope opposite Erden. Its Rieslings are firmer and more mineral than the Prälat, with blue slate and citrus. Dr. Loosen, Mönchhof, Markus Molitor and Jos. Christoffel make classic wines here. Erden sits on the inside of a bend, so its great vineyards lie across the river; Dr. Loosen's Treppchen Grosses Gewächs, from old own-rooted vines, is often the most mineral wine of his range.
de-erden-treppchen.terroir: About 36 ha of grey-blue Devonian slate on a very steep, south-west-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Schwarzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 36.3 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Erden include Busslay and Prälat.

de-filzen-altenberg.name: Altenberg
de-filzen-altenberg.summary: The Kanzemer Altenberg is one of the steepest and most dramatic slopes on the Saar, a wall of slate rising directly from the river opposite Kanzem. Von Othegraven, owned since 2010 by the television presenter Günther Jauch, whose family has roots in the estate, is the reference grower; Van Volxem and the Bischöfliche Weingüter also bottle it. The wines are powerful by Saar standards, with yellow fruit, smoke and a long stony finish, and the dry Grosses Gewächs ages superbly.
de-filzen-altenberg.terroir: Around 19 ha of grey and blue slate with weathered diabase, pitched up to about 70 percent and facing south-south-west straight over the water, which reflects light and moderates frost. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 19.1 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Filzen include Pulchen.
de-filzen-altenberg.nerd_note: Clotten's 1868 tax map did not list the Altenberg among the top Saar sites; its fame grew later, as Lars Carlberg's study of the map points out.

de-filzen-pulchen.name: Filzener Pulchen
de-filzen-pulchen.summary: A small, steep site in Filzen, the Pulchen is the home vineyard of Weingut Piedmont and gives fine, lively Saar Riesling.
de-filzen-pulchen.terroir: Slate on a south-east-facing slope above the lower Saar. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 2.3 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Filzen include Altenberg.

de-forst-elster.name: Forster Elster
de-forst-elster.summary: A Forst site of about 8 ha, giving ripe, aromatic Riesling.
de-forst-elster.terroir: Sandy loam with basalt fragments. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 7.7 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Forst include Ungeheuer, Pechstein, Jesuitengarten and Freundstück.

de-forst-freundstuck.name: Forster Freundstück
de-forst-freundstuck.summary: A small Forst site of about 3.5 ha next to the Kirchenstück, giving fine, mineral Riesling, notably from von Buhl.
de-forst-freundstuck.terroir: Sandstone, limestone and basalt rubble. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 3.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Forst include Ungeheuer, Pechstein, Elster and Jesuitengarten.

de-forst-jesuitengarten.name: Forster Jesuitengarten
de-forst-jesuitengarten.summary: The Jesuitengarten was a property of the Jesuits until their order was suppressed in 1773. This small, walled Forst site gives aromatic, elegant Riesling, slightly more open than the Kirchenstück. Bassermann-Jordan, von Buhl, Bürklin-Wolf and von Winning make reference wines. Forst's four grand sites, Kirchenstück, Jesuitengarten, Pechstein and Ungeheuer, lie side by side along barely two kilometres of hillside, which makes Forst the classic place to taste how basalt, limestone and sandstone change Riesling.
de-forst-jesuitengarten.terroir: About 7 ha of sandy loam with basalt and limestone fragments on a gentle east-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 6.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Forst include Ungeheuer, Pechstein, Elster and Freundstück.

de-forst-kirchenstuck.name: Forster Kirchenstück
de-forst-kirchenstuck.summary: The Kirchenstück is a walled, almost flat vineyard of about 3.6 ha behind the church in Forst, and by price and reputation the greatest site of the Pfalz. Its Rieslings are not loud but complete: silky, multilayered, with citrus, white flowers and a long, salty finish. The Bavarian land-tax survey of the Palatinate in 1828 already valued it above every other Forst site. Bürklin-Wolf, von Buhl, Bassermann-Jordan, Mosbacher and Acham-Magin share it.
de-forst-kirchenstuck.terroir: A complex mix of sandstone, limestone and basalt rubble washed down from the Pechsteinkopf, on a gentle east-facing slope at about 130 m, sheltered by the Haardt hills and the walls of the village. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 3.6 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Forst include Ungeheuer, Pechstein, Elster and Jesuitengarten.
de-forst-kirchenstuck.nerd_note: Bürklin-Wolf labels its Kirchenstück 'G.C.' (grand cru) under a Burgundy-inspired estate classification it adopted in the 1990s, before the VDP built its own pyramid.

de-forst-pechstein.name: Forster Pechstein
de-forst-pechstein.summary: The Pechstein ('pitch stone') takes its name from black basalt, the remnant of an extinct volcano, the Pechsteinkopf, above Forst. The dark stones absorb heat, and the Rieslings are smoky, spicy and taut, the most mineral of the Forst grand sites. Bürklin-Wolf, von Winning, Mosbacher and von Buhl lead.
de-forst-pechstein.terroir: About 16 ha of basalt rubble over sandy loam, on a gentle slope facing east. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 15.7 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Forst include Ungeheuer, Elster, Jesuitengarten and Freundstück.
de-forst-pechstein.nerd_note: Basalt from the Pechsteinkopf was quarried for centuries and, by local tradition, spread in neighbouring Forst vineyards to darken and warm the soil.

de-forst-ungeheuer.name: Forster Ungeheuer
de-forst-ungeheuer.summary: The Ungeheuer ('monster') is the largest of Forst's grand sites, about 33 ha. Otto von Bismarck is said to have remarked that the monster tasted very good. Its Rieslings are full, ripe and spicy, with power and grip from basalt and limestone. As the largest of the four Forst grand sites, it is also the easiest to find and often the best introduction to the village.
de-forst-ungeheuer.terroir: Basalt, limestone and sandstone rubble on gentle east-facing slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 33 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Forst include Pechstein, Elster, Jesuitengarten and Freundstück.
de-forst-ungeheuer.nerd_note: The name is usually traced to a local family called Ungeheuer, not to any beast.

de-frankweiler-kalkgrube.name: Frankweilerer Kalkgrube
de-frankweiler-kalkgrube.summary: A Frankweiler site of about 96 ha on limestone, giving fresh white wines and Pinot.
de-frankweiler-kalkgrube.terroir: Limestone and loess. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Südl. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Königsgarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 95.6 ha are registered under vine.

de-gimmeldingen-mandelgarten.name: Mandelgarten
de-gimmeldingen-mandelgarten.summary: The Mandelgarten, shared by Gimmeldingen and Mussbach, is lined with almond trees that blossom in March, the first sign of spring along the German Wine Route. Christmann makes an elegant, floral Riesling here.
de-gimmeldingen-mandelgarten.terroir: About 26 ha of sandy loam and sandstone. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Meerspinne (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 25.7 ha are registered under vine.

de-gleisweiler-holle.name: Gleisweilerer Hölle
de-gleisweiler-holle.summary: A Gleisweiler site of about 58 ha in a warm hollow, giving ripe Riesling and Pinot from Minges and others.
de-gleisweiler-holle.terroir: Sandstone, loam and limestone. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Südl. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Bischofskreuz (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 57.6 ha are registered under vine.

de-godramstein-munzberg.name: Godramsteiner Münzberg
de-godramstein-munzberg.summary: A very large Godramstein site of about 430 ha, whose name was taken by Weingut Münzberg, known for Pinot.
de-godramstein-munzberg.terroir: Loess, limestone and loam. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Südl. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Königsgarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 433.5 ha are registered under vine.

de-graach-abtsberg.name: Graacher Abtsberg
de-graach-abtsberg.summary: A small, historic part of the Graach hillside once owned by St. Martin's abbey in Trier, bottled separately by a few estates.
de-graach-abtsberg.terroir: Steep slate next to the Domprobst. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Münzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 2.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Graach include Himmelreich, Domprobst and Josephshöfer.

de-graach-domprobst.name: Graacher Domprobst
de-graach-domprobst.summary: The Domprobst is Graach's steepest and most mineral site, named for the provost of Trier cathedral who once owned it. Willi Schaefer's fruity-sweet Kabinett and Spätlese from here are cult wines, with intense slate, citrus and herb flavours and a cool, pure finish; Kees-Kieren, Markus Molitor and S.A. Prüm also excel.
de-graach-domprobst.terroir: About 18 ha of deep blue and grey Devonian slate on a slope of up to 70 percent, south-west facing, with very thin topsoil that keeps yields low. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Münzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 17.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Graach include Himmelreich, Abtsberg and Josephshöfer.
de-graach-domprobst.nerd_note: The old parcel name 'Graacher Abtsberg' within the slope recalls the abbey of St. Martin in Trier.

de-graach-himmelreich.name: Graacher Himmelreich
de-graach-himmelreich.summary: Graach's large Himmelreich ('kingdom of heaven'), about 57 ha, runs between the Domprobst and the Wehlener Sonnenuhr and gives some of the most charming fruity-sweet Kabinetts of the Mosel. Joh. Jos. Prüm, Dr. Loosen, Willi Schaefer and Selbach-Oster are reference growers. It is a classic source of the Mosel Kabinett archetype: around 8 percent alcohol, sweetness held in check by acidity, and flavours of green apple, white peach and wet slate.
de-graach-himmelreich.terroir: Grey slate with more weathered loam than the Domprobst, giving softer, rounder wines on slopes facing south-west. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Münzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 57.3 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Graach include Domprobst, Abtsberg and Josephshöfer.

de-graach-josephshofer.name: Josephshöfer
de-graach-josephshofer.summary: The Josephshöfer is the monopole of Reichsgraf von Kesselstatt, a walled site around the Josephshof manor between Graach and Wehlen that Kesselstatt acquired in the mid-nineteenth century. It gives full, ripe and spicy Riesling, slightly broader in build than the Sonnenuhr next door. Kesselstatt bottles it under the site name alone, from Kabinett to Grosses Gewächs, a rare case of a Mosel vineyard name standing without its village.
de-graach-josephshofer.terroir: Deep weathered slate on a steep south-west-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Münzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Graach include Himmelreich, Domprobst and Abtsberg.

de-grosskarlbach-burgweg.name: Großkarlbacher Burgweg
de-grosskarlbach-burgweg.summary: A large Grosskarlbach site whose best parcels give dense Riesling and Pinot Noir from Knipser and Philipp Kuhn.
de-grosskarlbach-burgweg.terroir: Limestone and loess. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Schwarzerde (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 128.1 ha are registered under vine.

de-guls-rottgen.name: Röttgen
de-guls-rottgen.summary: The Röttgen, shared by Winningen and Güls, is a steep terraced site whose Rieslings are spicy and complex, made famously dry by Heymann-Löwenstein and Knebel.
de-guls-rottgen.terroir: About 10.6 ha of slate terraces, south-facing. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Burg Cochem and the Grosslage Weinhex (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 10.6 ha are registered under vine.

de-haardt-burgergarten.name: Haardter Bürgergarten
de-haardt-burgergarten.summary: The Bürgergarten at Haardt includes the parcel 'im Breumel', the source of Müller-Catoir's Grosses Gewächs: aromatic, floral and filigree Riesling.
de-haardt-burgergarten.terroir: About 18 ha of sandstone and loam at the foot of the Haardt hills. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Meerspinne (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 18.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Haardt include Herrenletten.

de-haardt-herrenletten.name: Haardter Herrenletten
de-haardt-herrenletten.summary: A Haardt site of about 15 ha near Neustadt, giving full, aromatic Riesling and Rieslaner from Müller-Catoir.
de-haardt-herrenletten.terroir: Loam and clay ('Letten') on a gentle slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Meerspinne (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 14.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Haardt include Bürgergarten.

de-hatzenport-kirchberg.name: Hatzenporter Kirchberg
de-hatzenport-kirchberg.summary: The Kirchberg rises behind the church at Hatzenport, a steep, terraced slope where Heymann-Löwenstein makes a dense, spicy dry Riesling. It sits on the Terrassenmosel, the lowest stretch of the Mosel, where dry-stone terraces are the only way to hold soil on the rock.
de-hatzenport-kirchberg.terroir: About 5.7 ha of terraced Devonian slate and sandstone, south-facing. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Burg Cochem and the Grosslage Weinhex (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 5.7 ha are registered under vine.

de-heimersheim-burggarten.name: Burggarten
de-heimersheim-burggarten.summary: A lower Ahr site of about 14 ha at Heimersheim with loess soils, giving softer, fruity Pinot Noir.
de-heimersheim-burggarten.terroir: Loess and loam near the mouth of the valley. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Walporzheim/Ahrtal and the Grosslage Klosterberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 14.4 ha are registered under vine.

de-hohen-sulzen-kirchenstuck.name: Hohen-Sülzener Kirchenstück
de-hohen-sulzen-kirchenstuck.summary: The Kirchenstück at Hohen-Sülzen is a limestone site that Battenfeld-Spanier has made famous with taut, saline dry Riesling.
de-hohen-sulzen-kirchenstuck.terroir: About 98 ha registered, limestone and marl on south-facing slopes on the border with the Pfalz. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Wonnegau and the Grosslage Domblick (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 98.3 ha are registered under vine.

de-ilbesheim-sonnenberg.name: Sonnenberg
de-ilbesheim-sonnenberg.summary: A large site shared by Ilbesheim and Leinsweiler, giving fresh Riesling and Pinot, with Siegrist among the best growers.
de-ilbesheim-sonnenberg.terroir: Limestone, loess and sandstone. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Südl. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Herrlich (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 120 ha are registered under vine.

de-kallstadt-saumagen.name: Kallstadter Saumagen
de-kallstadt-saumagen.summary: The Saumagen is a former Roman limestone quarry above Kallstadt, named after its shape like a pig's stomach (also a Palatinate dish). Koehler-Ruprecht's Rieslings from here, made in an old-fashioned way in large casks, are legendary for their longevity. The wines are powerful and chalky, with a salty finish.
de-kallstadt-saumagen.terroir: About 40 ha of limestone and marl on a south-east-facing slope, very warm and dry. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Kobnert (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 39.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Kallstadt include Steinacker.
de-kallstadt-saumagen.nerd_note: Kallstadt is also the ancestral village of the Trump and Heinz families, a coincidence locals mention with mixed feelings.

de-kallstadt-steinacker.name: Kallstadter Steinacker
de-kallstadt-steinacker.summary: A large Kallstadt site of about 123 ha on limestone, giving rich Riesling and Pinot, with some top parcels.
de-kallstadt-steinacker.terroir: Limestone and loam. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Kobnert (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 122.6 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Kallstadt include Saumagen.

de-kanzem-horecker.name: Kanzemer Hörecker
de-kanzem-horecker.summary: A tiny, historic Kanzem site, the Hörecker was once among the most expensive vineyards of the Saar and is today a rarity bottled by only a few estates.
de-kanzem-horecker.terroir: Steep slate pocket close to the Altenberg. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Kanzem include Sonnenberg.

de-kanzem-sonnenberg.name: Kanzemer Sonnenberg
de-kanzem-sonnenberg.summary: Kanzem's broad Sonnenberg (about 20 ha) runs along the right bank of the Saar and gives lighter, fragrant Riesling, often made fruity-sweet in the Kabinett style.
de-kanzem-sonnenberg.terroir: Slate and loam on moderately steep south-west slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 19.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Kanzem include Hörecker.

de-kasel-hitzlay.name: Kaseler Hitzlay
de-kasel-hitzlay.summary: Kasel's Hitzlay ('heat rock') is a warm pocket of slate giving riper, more aromatic Ruwer Riesling than its cooler neighbours.
de-kasel-hitzlay.terroir: Slate outcrop that reflects and stores heat. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Ruwer and belongs to no Grosslage; about 8.3 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Kasel include Kehrnagel and Nies'chen.

de-kasel-kehrnagel.name: Kaseler Kehrnagel
de-kasel-kehrnagel.summary: A steep Kasel site of about 11 ha, the Kehrnagel gives racy, citrus-scented Riesling, notably for Reichsgraf von Kesselstatt.
de-kasel-kehrnagel.terroir: Grey slate on a south-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Ruwer and belongs to no Grosslage; about 10.7 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Kasel include Hitzlay and Nies'chen.

de-kasel-nies-chen.name: Kaseler Nies'chen
de-kasel-nies-chen.summary: The Nies'chen is Kasel's finest slope, a steep amphitheatre of blue slate whose Rieslings are perfumed, delicate and chalky-fine. Reichsgraf von Kesselstatt, Erben von Beulwitz and the Bischöfliche Weingüter all make benchmark fruity-sweet and dry wines here. The Ruwer is so narrow and cool that its Rieslings are often the lightest of the whole Mosel, with Kabinetts of 7.5 to 8.5 percent alcohol quite normal, and the Nies'chen's blue slate adds a floral, almost violet lift.
de-kasel-nies-chen.terroir: About 14 ha of blue Devonian slate on a south-west-facing slope in the cool Ruwer valley. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Ruwer and belongs to no Grosslage; about 14.1 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Kasel include Hitzlay and Kehrnagel.

de-kesten-paulinshofberger.name: Kestener Paulinshofberger
de-kesten-paulinshofberger.summary: A Kesten site of about 18 ha named after the Paulinshof, a former property of St. Paulinus in Trier. Weingut Paulinshof and Fritz Haag make fine Riesling here.
de-kesten-paulinshofberger.terroir: Slate on a south-facing slope opposite the Brauneberg. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Kurfürstlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 17.9 ha are registered under vine.

de-kinheim-rosenberg.name: Kinheimer Rosenberg
de-kinheim-rosenberg.summary: A Kinheim slope of about 44 ha, giving lively, fruity Riesling of good value.
de-kinheim-rosenberg.terroir: Slate on moderately steep slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Schwarzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 44.1 ha are registered under vine.

de-kloerath-bruderschaft.name: Klöerather Bruderschaft
de-kloerath-bruderschaft.summary: Klüsserath's Bruderschaft is a long, steep slope of about 186 ha, revived by growers such as Kirsten and Friedrich-Wilhelm-Gymnasium, giving bright, mineral Riesling.
de-kloerath-bruderschaft.terroir: Slate on a south-facing curve of the river. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Sankt Michael (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 186.2 ha are registered under vine.

de-kobern-uhlen.name: Uhlen
de-kobern-uhlen.summary: The Uhlen is the great site of Winningen, a long, terraced cliff above the lower Mosel. Reinhard Löwenstein of Heymann-Löwenstein argued for decades that its three sections have different rocks and should be named separately; the EU now protects Uhlen Blaufüßer Lay, Uhlen Laubach and Uhlen Roth Lay as designations of their own. The wines are dense, often powerful dry Rieslings with smoke, herbs and a salty finish. Knebel and Lubentiushof also excel.
de-kobern-uhlen.terroir: About 14 ha registered under vine on steep terraces of Devonian slate: blue slate in the Blaufüßer Lay, fossil-rich grey slate and limestone bands in the Laubach, red iron-rich slate in the Roth Lay. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Burg Cochem and the Grosslage Weinhex (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 14.4 ha are registered under vine.
de-kobern-uhlen.nerd_note: The fossil beds of the Laubach section contain Devonian marine creatures, a reminder that the slate began as ocean mud around 400 million years ago.

de-konigsbach-idig.name: Königsbacher Idig
de-konigsbach-idig.summary: The Idig is a limestone site at Königsbach near Neustadt that Steffen Christmann made into one of the leading Grosse Gewächse of the Pfalz, both for Riesling and Pinot Noir. The Riesling is powerful, chalky and long. Christmann converted to biodynamic farming in the 2000s, and Steffen Christmann served for many years as president of the VDP, shaping its classification of Grosse Lagen.
de-konigsbach-idig.terroir: About 16 ha of limestone and marl with some sandstone rubble on a south-east-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Meerspinne (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 16.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Königsbach include Ölberg.

de-konigsbach-olberg.name: Königsbacher Ölberg
de-konigsbach-olberg.summary: A Königsbach site of about 28 ha giving ripe, mineral Riesling, notably from Christmann.
de-konigsbach-olberg.terroir: Limestone and sandstone. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Meerspinne (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 28.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Königsbach include Idig.

de-kurenz-altenberg.name: Kürenzer Altenberg
de-kurenz-altenberg.summary: A Trier site on the slopes of Kürenz and Avelsbach, near the vineyards the Prussian state domain developed in the late nineteenth century. It gives fine, cool Riesling within sight of the city.
de-kurenz-altenberg.terroir: Slate slopes at the mouth of the Ruwer and Avelsbach valleys. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Römerlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages).

de-langenlonsheim-konigsschild.name: Langenlonsheimer Königsschild
de-langenlonsheim-konigsschild.summary: A Langenlonsheim site of about 15 ha, giving bright, fruity Riesling, notably for Tesch's single-vineyard range.
de-langenlonsheim-konigsschild.terroir: Loam over gravel and quartzite. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Schlosskapelle (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 15.1 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Langenlonsheim include Rothenberg.

de-langenlonsheim-rothenberg.name: Langenlonsheimer Rothenberg
de-langenlonsheim-rothenberg.summary: A Langenlonsheim slope of about 10 ha with red, iron-rich soils, giving warm, spicy Riesling from Tesch and others.
de-langenlonsheim-rothenberg.terroir: Red sandstone and loam (Rotliegend) on a south-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Schlosskapelle (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 9.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Langenlonsheim include Königsschild.

de-laubenheim-karthauser.name: Laubenheimer Karthäuser
de-laubenheim-karthauser.summary: A Laubenheim site of about 18 ha once owned by Carthusian monks, made famous by Martin Tesch with taut, unadorned dry Riesling.
de-laubenheim-karthauser.terroir: Weathered quartzite and loam on south-facing slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Schlosskapelle (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 18.4 ha are registered under vine.

de-laumersheim-kirschgarten.name: Laumersheimer Kirschgarten
de-laumersheim-kirschgarten.summary: The Kirschgarten at Laumersheim is one of the best Pinot Noir sites in Germany, made famous by Knipser and Philipp Kuhn. The wines are deep, structured and age-worthy. Werner and Volker Knipser were among the first in Germany to age Pinot Noir in new barriques in the 1980s, and the northern Pfalz limestone proved ideal for it.
de-laumersheim-kirschgarten.terroir: About 47 ha of limestone and marl, south facing, at the northern end of the Pfalz. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Schwarzerde (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 47.3 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Laumersheim include Steinbuckel.

de-laumersheim-steinbuckel.name: Laumersheimer Steinbuckel
de-laumersheim-steinbuckel.summary: A Laumersheim site of about 62 ha on limestone where Philipp Kuhn and Knipser grow Riesling and Pinot.
de-laumersheim-steinbuckel.terroir: Limestone and loess. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Schwarzerde (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 62.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Laumersheim include Kirschgarten.

de-lehmen-wurzlay.name: Lehmener Würzlay
de-lehmen-wurzlay.summary: A small terraced Lehmen site of about 6 ha, giving spicy, ripe Riesling.
de-lehmen-wurzlay.terroir: Slate terraces on the lower Mosel. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Burg Cochem and the Grosslage Weinhex (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 5.9 ha are registered under vine.

de-leiwen-klostergarten.name: Leiwener Klostergarten
de-leiwen-klostergarten.summary: A large, flatter Leiwen site of about 240 ha giving everyday Riesling and Müller-Thurgau; Carl Loewen makes a fine old-vine wine from a better parcel.
de-leiwen-klostergarten.terroir: Gravel and loam on the inside of the river bend. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Sankt Michael (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 240.3 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Leiwen include Laurentiuslay.

de-leiwen-laurentiuslay.name: Leiwener Laurentiuslay
de-leiwen-laurentiuslay.summary: The Laurentiuslay is Leiwen's great slope, crowned by a small chapel of St. Lawrence on a rocky ridge across the river from the village.
