Grans-Fassian, Carl Loewen and Sankt Urbans-Hof make powerful, spicy dry Rieslings and luscious Auslesen here; the site's old vines give density without heaviness.
de-leiwen-laurentiuslay.terroir: About 16 ha of grey and blue slate with quartzite, very steep, facing south and south-west over the Mosel. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Sankt Michael (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 16.1 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Leiwen include Klostergarten.
de-leiwen-laurentiuslay.nerd_note: Leiwen was known for volume production on the flats after the 1970s land consolidations; the Laurentiuslay helped growers like Gerhard Grans prove the village's steep slopes could rank with the best.

de-leutesdorf-gartenlay.name: Leutesdorfer Gartenlay
de-leutesdorf-gartenlay.summary: A Leutesdorf site of about 45 ha on the lower Middle Rhine, giving lively Riesling and some Pinot Noir.
de-leutesdorf-gartenlay.terroir: Slate and loess on south-facing slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Loreley and the Grosslage Burg Hammerstein (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 44.8 ha are registered under vine.

de-lieser-niederberg-helden.name: Lieserer Niederberg-Helden
de-lieser-niederberg-helden.summary: The Niederberg-Helden is a steep south-facing slope above Lieser that Thomas Haag of Schloss Lieser has restored to prominence. Its Riesling is spicy and powerful, with a cool blue-slate thread. Schloss Lieser, the neo-Gothic manor in the village, was revived after Thomas Haag, son of Wilhelm Haag of Fritz Haag, took over as winemaker in 1992; his family later bought the estate. The 1971 law joined the historic Niederberg and Helden slopes into one Einzellage.
de-lieser-niederberg-helden.terroir: About 30 ha of blue and grey slate on a steep slope at the mouth of the Lieser valley. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Kurfürstlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 29.9 ha are registered under vine.

de-longuich-maximiner-herrenberg.name: Longuicher Maximiner Herrenberg
de-longuich-maximiner-herrenberg.summary: This Longuich site was once owned by St. Maximin abbey in Trier. Carl Loewen holds a parcel of ungrafted Riesling planted in 1896, among the oldest productive vineyards in Germany, and bottles it as '1896'.
de-longuich-maximiner-herrenberg.terroir: About 12 ha of red slate and weathered sandstone on a south-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Probstberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 12.2 ha are registered under vine.
de-longuich-maximiner-herrenberg.nerd_note: The 1896 vines were planted at a time when Riesling cuttings were still propagated by massal selection from the slope itself.

de-mayschoss-laacherberg.name: Mayschoßer Laacherberg
de-mayschoss-laacherberg.summary: A steep Mayschoss site of about 15 ha named after Maria Laach abbey, which owned vineyards here, giving spicy Pinot Noir.
de-mayschoss-laacherberg.terroir: Slate and greywacke. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Walporzheim/Ahrtal and the Grosslage Klosterberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 15.3 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Mayschoß include Mönchberg.

de-mayschoss-monchberg.name: Mayschoßer Mönchberg
de-mayschoss-monchberg.summary: The Mönchberg at Mayschoss is a steep slate slope once owned by monks, giving elegant Pinot Noir. Deutzerhof and the Mayschoss cooperative, founded in 1868 and the oldest wine cooperative in Germany, work here.
de-mayschoss-monchberg.terroir: About 60 ha of slate and greywacke on steep slopes above a loop of the Ahr. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Walporzheim/Ahrtal and the Grosslage Klosterberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 60.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Mayschoß include Laacherberg.

de-meddersheim-rheingrafenberg.name: Meddersheimer Rheingrafenberg
de-meddersheim-rheingrafenberg.summary: A Meddersheim site of about 28 ha, named after the Rhinegraves who ruled the area, giving fresh, fruity Riesling, notably for the local cooperative and family estates.
de-meddersheim-rheingrafenberg.terroir: Volcanic and sandstone soils on south-facing slopes of the upper Nahe. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Paradiesgarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 28.4 ha are registered under vine.

de-mertesdorf-abtsberg.name: Mertesdorfer Abtsberg
de-mertesdorf-abtsberg.summary: The Abtsberg is the jewel of Maximin Grünhaus, the walled estate at the foot of a steep slope in the Ruwer valley that Emperor Otto I gave to St. Maximin abbey of Trier in 966. Monks worked it until Napoleon's secularisation; the von Schubert family has owned it since 1882. Abtsberg Rieslings are delicate and intensely mineral, with blackcurrant leaf, citrus and a lingering blue-slate finish, magnificent both dry and fruity-sweet.
de-mertesdorf-abtsberg.terroir: Blue Devonian slate on a south to south-east-facing slope up to about 70 percent, in a narrow, cool side valley where Rieslings ripen late and keep high acidity. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Ruwer and belongs to no Grosslage. Neighbouring sites in Mertesdorf include Herrenberg and Bruderberg.
de-mertesdorf-abtsberg.nerd_note: On Clotten's 1868 map the Abtsberg was shaded dark red but labelled Herrenberg; the estate's three sites (Abtsberg, Herrenberg, Bruderberg) were once allocated to the abbot, the monastery and the brothers.

de-mertesdorf-bruderberg.name: Mertesdorfer Bruderberg
de-mertesdorf-bruderberg.summary: The smallest of Maximin Grünhaus's three sites, the Bruderberg was historically the lay brothers' vineyard. It gives a firm, spicy Riesling bottled in small quantities.
de-mertesdorf-bruderberg.terroir: Iron-rich slate on a steep, south-facing slope at the downstream end of the Grünhaus hill. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Ruwer and belongs to no Grosslage. Neighbouring sites in Mertesdorf include Herrenberg and Abtsberg.

de-mertesdorf-herrenberg.name: Mertesdorfer Herrenberg
de-mertesdorf-herrenberg.summary: The second great site of Maximin Grünhaus, the Herrenberg lies just downstream of the Abtsberg on red-tinged slate. Its wines are broader and fruitier, with ripe apricot and spice, and the estate also grows Pinot Noir here. The von Schubert family still runs the estate; the Herrenberg's Kabinett is often the most approachable of the three Grünhaus sites when young, while its Auslesen turn honeyed and spicy over twenty years.
de-mertesdorf-herrenberg.terroir: About 28 ha (registered vine area) of red and grey slate with more iron, slightly warmer than the Abtsberg. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Ruwer and belongs to no Grosslage; about 28.2 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Mertesdorf include Abtsberg and Bruderberg.
de-mertesdorf-herrenberg.nerd_note: In monastic times the Herrenberg's wine went to the 'Herren', the monks of St. Maximin.

de-molsheim-zellerweg-am-schwarzen-herrg.name: Mölsheimer Zellerweg am Schwarzen Herrgott
de-molsheim-zellerweg-am-schwarzen-herrg.summary: This site with one of Germany's longest vineyard names, 'the Zell path by the black crucifix', lies at Mölsheim on the border with the Pfalz. Battenfeld-Spanier makes a cool, limestone-driven Riesling here.
de-molsheim-zellerweg-am-schwarzen-herrg.terroir: About 56 ha of limestone on a high plateau. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Wonnegau and the Grosslage Domblick (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 55.8 ha are registered under vine.

de-monzingen-fruhlingsplatzchen.name: Monzingener Frühlingsplätzchen
de-monzingen-fruhlingsplatzchen.summary: The Frühlingsplätzchen ('little spring place') is Monzingen's second great site, warmer and softer than the Halenberg, with red slate and loam. Emrich-Schönleber's wines from here are juicy and generous.
de-monzingen-fruhlingsplatzchen.terroir: About 70 ha registered, red slate, quartzite and loam on south-facing slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Paradiesgarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 69.7 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Monzingen include Halenberg.
de-monzingen-fruhlingsplatzchen.nerd_note: The name refers to the early bud-break of this sheltered slope.

de-monzingen-halenberg.name: Monzingener Halenberg
de-monzingen-halenberg.summary: The Halenberg is the great site of Emrich-Schönleber, a very steep slope above Monzingen on the upper Nahe. Its blue slate and quartzite give some of Germany's most electric dry Rieslings: cool, smoky, salty and very long, plus spectacular sweet wines. Schönleber's Halenberg GG is regularly cited among the best dry Rieslings of the country.
de-monzingen-halenberg.terroir: About 8 ha of blue Devonian slate with quartzite on a south-facing slope of up to 70 percent, higher and cooler than the middle Nahe. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Paradiesgarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 8.3 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Monzingen include Frühlingsplätzchen.
de-monzingen-halenberg.nerd_note: Monzingen lies on the edge of the Hunsrück; the cool winds and the slate give the Halenberg a Mosel-like nerve with Nahe depth.

de-mulheim-helenenkloster.name: Mülheimer Helenenkloster
de-mulheim-helenenkloster.summary: A small monopole of Max Ferd. Richter in Mülheim, the Helenenkloster is famous for Eiswein, which the estate has made here in many years.
de-mulheim-helenenkloster.terroir: A cool site where early frosts let the estate freeze grapes on the vine in many winters. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Kurfürstlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages).

de-munster-sarmsheim-dautenpflanzer.name: Münster-Sarmsheimer Dautenpflänzer
de-munster-sarmsheim-dautenpflanzer.summary: A small, steep site of about 4 ha in Münster-Sarmsheim at the mouth of the Nahe, where Kruger-Rumpf makes a spicy, mineral Riesling with real tension.
de-munster-sarmsheim-dautenpflanzer.terroir: Slate and quartzite on a steep south-facing slope near the Rhine. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Schlosskapelle (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Münster-Sarmsheim include Pittersberg.

de-munster-sarmsheim-pittersberg.name: Münster-Sarmsheimer Pittersberg
de-munster-sarmsheim-pittersberg.summary: A Münster-Sarmsheim site of about 9 ha of blue slate giving cool, elegant Riesling, notably from Kruger-Rumpf.
de-munster-sarmsheim-pittersberg.terroir: Blue slate on a steep slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Schlosskapelle (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 9.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Münster-Sarmsheim include Dautenpflänzer.

de-nackenheim-rothenberg.name: Nackenheimer Rothenberg
de-nackenheim-rothenberg.summary: The Rothenberg is the northern end of the Roter Hang at Nackenheim, the steepest and reddest of its slopes. Gunderloch made it famous in the 1990s with spectacular sweet Rieslings, and Kühling-Gillot farms ungrafted vines here. The wines are intense, spicy and long-lived. Nackenheim is the birthplace of the playwright Carl Zuckmayer, whose comedy 'Der fröhliche Weinberg' (1925) is set among Rheinhessen vineyards.
de-nackenheim-rothenberg.terroir: About 14.5 ha of red Rotliegend clay-slate on steep east-facing slopes above the Rhine. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nierstein and the Grosslage Spiegelberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 14.5 ha are registered under vine.
de-nackenheim-rothenberg.nerd_note: Kühling-Gillot still farms very old own-rooted vines here, rare on the Rhine.

de-neef-petersberg.name: Neefer Petersberg
de-neef-petersberg.summary: A small, steep Neef site under the chapel of St. Peter, giving firm, mineral Riesling.
de-neef-petersberg.terroir: Slate on a south-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Burg Cochem and the Grosslage Grafschaft (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 7.7 ha are registered under vine.

de-neu-bamberg-heerkretz.name: Heerkretz
de-neu-bamberg-heerkretz.summary: The Heerkretz, shared by Siefersheim and Neu-Bamberg, is a steep, rocky slope of porphyry giving intense, smoky Riesling, the flagship of Wagner-Stempel. Daniel Wagner of Wagner-Stempel turned these remote western hills of Rheinhessen into a Grosses Gewächs address; the porphyry gives a smoky, saline character closer to the Nahe than to the limestone of the Wonnegau.
de-neu-bamberg-heerkretz.terroir: About 58 ha of rhyolite rock and thin soils on south-facing slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bingen and the Grosslage Rheingrafenstein (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 58.2 ha are registered under vine.

de-neumagen-laudamusberg.name: Neumagener Laudamusberg
de-neumagen-laudamusberg.summary: A steep Neumagen slope of about 22 ha, giving firm, slatey Riesling.
de-neumagen-laudamusberg.terroir: Grey slate on the left bank. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Michelsberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 22.3 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Neumagen include Rosengärtchen.

de-neumagen-rosengartchen.name: Neumagener Rosengärtchen
de-neumagen-rosengartchen.summary: A Neumagen site of about 23 ha, close to the place where the stone relief of a Roman wine ship was found in 1878. It gives lively, medium-weight Riesling.
de-neumagen-rosengartchen.terroir: Slate and loam on south-facing slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Michelsberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 22.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Neumagen include Laudamusberg.

de-nieder-florsheim-frauenberg.name: Nieder-Flörsheimer Frauenberg
de-nieder-florsheim-frauenberg.summary: The Frauenberg at Nieder-Flörsheim is a high limestone hill where Keller and Battenfeld-Spanier grow cool, precise Riesling and Pinot Noir.
de-nieder-florsheim-frauenberg.terroir: Limestone with little soil on a high, windy plateau edge. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Wonnegau and the Grosslage Burg Rodenstein (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 150.2 ha are registered under vine.

de-nieder-ingelheim-horn.name: Horn
de-nieder-ingelheim-horn.summary: The Horn, shared by Nieder- and Ober-Ingelheim, gives fine Pinot Noir on limestone, notably from J. Neus.
de-nieder-ingelheim-horn.terroir: About 21 ha of limestone and loess. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bingen and the Grosslage Kaiserpfalz (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 21.4 ha are registered under vine.

de-niederhausen-hermannsberg.name: Niederhausener Hermannsberg
de-niederhausen-hermannsberg.summary: The Hermannsberg is the monopole of Gut Hermannsberg, founded in 1902 as the Prussian State Domain at Niederhausen. Labourers, including prisoners, blasted terraces out of the rock to create model vineyards, and the estate was one of Germany's most famous until its decline after the 1990s; new owners have restored it since 2009. The Riesling is powerful, spicy and stony.
de-niederhausen-hermannsberg.terroir: Volcanic rock and slate terraces on a steep slope above the Nahe. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Burgweg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Niederhausen include Klamm, Hermannshöhle, Rosenheck and Steinberg.
de-niederhausen-hermannsberg.nerd_note: The domain's wines were the Prussian state's showcase for what scientific viticulture could do on abandoned slopes.

de-niederhausen-hermannshohle.name: Niederhausener Hermannshöhle
de-niederhausen-hermannshohle.summary: The Hermannshöhle is the Nahe's most celebrated vineyard, a steep, south-facing slope above the river at Niederhausen where an astonishing mix of rocks meets in a few hectares. Helmut and Cornelius Dönnhoff made it famous worldwide, and their Grosses Gewächs and fruity-sweet Spätlese from here combine Mosel-like delicacy with a deeper, spicier, more mineral core. Jakob Schneider and Gut Hermannsberg also own parcels. Prussian-era tax classifications of the Nahe already placed it in the top class.
de-niederhausen-hermannshohle.terroir: About 8.4 ha under vine on grey slate interleaved with volcanic porphyry (rhyolite), melaphyre and bands of limestone; the slope faces south and south-west over the Nahe, which reflects light and keeps frost away. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Burgweg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 8.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Niederhausen include Klamm, Hermannsberg, Rosenheck and Steinberg.
de-niederhausen-hermannshohle.nerd_note: Few vineyards anywhere pack so many rock types into so small an area, which helps explain why the Hermannshöhle tastes more layered than its neighbours.

de-niederhausen-klamm.name: Niederhausener Klamm
de-niederhausen-klamm.summary: A small Niederhausen site of about 7.5 ha in a narrow gorge ('Klamm'), giving taut, cool Riesling.
de-niederhausen-klamm.terroir: Slate and volcanic rock in a shaded side valley. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Burgweg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 7.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Niederhausen include Hermannsberg, Hermannshöhle, Rosenheck and Steinberg.

de-niederhausen-rosenheck.name: Niederhausener Rosenheck
de-niederhausen-rosenheck.summary: A Niederhausen site of about 9.6 ha above the river, giving fragrant, fine Riesling for several estates.
de-niederhausen-rosenheck.terroir: Porphyry and slate on a south-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Burgweg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 9.6 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Niederhausen include Klamm, Hermannsberg, Hermannshöhle and Steinberg.

de-niederhausen-steinberg.name: Niederhausener Steinberg
de-niederhausen-steinberg.summary: A Niederhausen site of about 5.6 ha that belongs in part to Gut Hermannsberg, giving firm, mineral Riesling.
de-niederhausen-steinberg.terroir: Volcanic and slate soils on a steep slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Burgweg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 5.6 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Niederhausen include Klamm, Hermannsberg, Hermannshöhle and Rosenheck.

de-nierstein-brudersberg.name: Niersteiner Brudersberg
de-nierstein-brudersberg.summary: The Brudersberg is a small, steep monopole on the Roter Hang, long the pride of the Heyl zu Herrnsheim estate and now worked by St. Antony. It gives firm, spicy Riesling.
de-nierstein-brudersberg.terroir: Red Rotliegend soils on a steep south-east slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nierstein and the Grosslage Rehbach (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Nierstein include Paterberg, Ölberg, Pettenthal and Hipping.

de-nierstein-glock.name: Niersteiner Glöck
de-nierstein-glock.summary: The Glöck is a small walled vineyard by St. Kilian's church in Nierstein, often called the oldest documented vineyard in Germany: a charter of 742 records its gift to the bishopric of Würzburg.
de-nierstein-glock.terroir: A walled urban site on loess and red soils. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nierstein and the Grosslage Auflangen (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Nierstein include Paterberg, Ölberg, Pettenthal and Hipping.
de-nierstein-glock.nerd_note: The 742 donation was made by Carloman, a son of Charles Martel.

de-nierstein-heiligenbaum.name: Niersteiner Heiligenbaum
de-nierstein-heiligenbaum.summary: A Nierstein site of about 12.5 ha named after a holy tree, giving lively, fruity Riesling.
de-nierstein-heiligenbaum.terroir: Red soils and loess on gentler slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nierstein and the Grosslage Auflangen (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 12.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Nierstein include Paterberg, Ölberg, Pettenthal and Hipping.

de-nierstein-hipping.name: Niersteiner Hipping
de-nierstein-hipping.summary: The Hipping is the heart of the Roter Hang right above Nierstein, a steep slope of red soil whose Rieslings are fine, spicy and long, a touch more elegant than the Pettenthal. Klaus Peter Keller's Hipping has become one of the most sought-after dry Rieslings of the Rhine; Schätzel and St. Antony also excel. In the nineteenth century the wines of Nierstein's red slope were sold at prices to rival the Rheingau's best, a reputation the 1971 Grosslage 'Niersteiner Gutes Domtal' did much to erode.
de-nierstein-hipping.terroir: About 23 ha of red Rotliegend clay-slate on an east to south-east-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nierstein and the Grosslage Rehbach (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 22.7 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Nierstein include Paterberg, Ölberg, Pettenthal and Heiligenbaum.

de-nierstein-olberg.name: Niersteiner Ölberg
de-nierstein-olberg.summary: The Ölberg ('olive hill') is a warm, steep slope in Nierstein that gives rich, round Riesling with ripe stone fruit, made by Keller, Schätzel, Huff and others.
de-nierstein-olberg.terroir: About 47 ha of red Rotliegend soils and some limestone, south-east facing. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nierstein and the Grosslage Auflangen (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 47.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Nierstein include Paterberg, Pettenthal, Hipping and Heiligenbaum.

de-nierstein-orbel.name: Orbel
de-nierstein-orbel.summary: The Orbel, shared by Nierstein and Schwabsburg, lies behind the Roter Hang on red soil and gives spicy, ripe Riesling.
de-nierstein-orbel.terroir: About 12 ha of Rotliegend soils. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nierstein and the Grosslage Auflangen (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 12.2 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Nierstein include Paterberg, Ölberg, Pettenthal and Hipping.

de-nierstein-paterberg.name: Niersteiner Paterberg
de-nierstein-paterberg.summary: A large Nierstein site of about 118 ha behind the town, giving ripe, everyday Riesling and Silvaner.
de-nierstein-paterberg.terroir: Loess and limestone on rolling slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nierstein and the Grosslage Spiegelberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 118.2 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Nierstein include Ölberg, Pettenthal, Hipping and Heiligenbaum.

de-nierstein-pettenthal.name: Niersteiner Pettenthal
de-nierstein-pettenthal.summary: The Pettenthal is the steepest and most famous part of the Roter Hang, the 'red slope' that runs along the Rhine north of Nierstein. Its Rieslings are exotic and dense, with peach, blood orange and a savoury, iron-tinged mineral finish. Kühling-Gillot, Keller, St. Antony, Gunderloch and Schätzel are among the owners; the wines rank with the finest dry Rieslings of Germany.
de-nierstein-pettenthal.terroir: About 30 ha of red Rotliegend clay-slate and siltstone (Permian, about 280 million years old) on slopes of up to 70 percent, facing east and south-east straight over the Rhine, which reflects morning light onto the vines. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nierstein and the Grosslage Rehbach (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 30.1 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Nierstein include Paterberg, Ölberg, Hipping and Heiligenbaum.
de-nierstein-pettenthal.nerd_note: The red rock was laid down in a hot desert basin; it crumbles into fine, iron-rich soil that warms quickly and drains well.

de-nittel-leiterchen.name: Nitteler Leiterchen
de-nittel-leiterchen.summary: The Leiterchen is the best-known site of the Upper Mosel, where the river forms the border with Luxembourg and Devonian slate gives way to Triassic shell limestone (Muschelkalk). It is a stronghold of Elbling, the ancient Roman-era variety of the area, giving crisp, citric still and sparkling wines.
de-nittel-leiterchen.terroir: About 38 ha of limestone and marl on south-facing slopes, a geology closer to Burgundy and Champagne than to the rest of the Mosel. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Obermosel and the Grosslage Gipfel (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 38.4 ha are registered under vine.
de-nittel-leiterchen.nerd_note: Elbling has been grown here for nearly 2,000 years; the Upper Mosel is its last real home in Germany.

de-norheim-dellchen.name: Norheimer Dellchen
de-norheim-dellchen.summary: The Dellchen is a steep, terraced slope of about 3 ha above Norheim, divided by dry-stone walls and rock outcrops. Dönnhoff's Grosses Gewächs from here is often his most aromatic, with white flowers, herbs and a cool, stony finish. Some terraces were abandoned in the late twentieth century because they could only be worked by hand; Dönnhoff and others have brought parcels back into production.
de-norheim-dellchen.terroir: Grey slate mixed with porphyry and melaphyre on small terraces facing south over the Nahe. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Burgweg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 3.1 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Norheim include Kafels and Kirschheck.

de-norheim-kafels.name: Norheimer Kafels
de-norheim-kafels.summary: The Kafels is a steep Norheim slope where volcanic rock dominates, giving spicy, mineral Riesling, for example from Jakob Schneider.
de-norheim-kafels.terroir: Volcanic soils on a south-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Burgweg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Norheim include Kirschheck and Dellchen.

de-norheim-kirschheck.name: Norheimer Kirschheck
de-norheim-kirschheck.summary: The Kirschheck in Norheim gives a lighter, fragrant style of Riesling; Dönnhoff's Kirschheck Spätlese is a byword for finesse.
de-norheim-kirschheck.terroir: About 13 ha of grey slate on a steep slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Burgweg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 13.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Norheim include Kafels and Dellchen.

de-ober-ingelheim-pares.name: Ober-Ingelheimer Pares
de-ober-ingelheim-pares.summary: The Pares at Ober-Ingelheim is a limestone site long celebrated for Pinot Noir; Ingelheim calls itself the 'red wine town' and its Spätburgunder tradition goes back to the Middle Ages. J. Neus is the reference producer.
de-ober-ingelheim-pares.terroir: About 9 ha of limestone and marl on south-facing slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bingen and the Grosslage Kaiserpfalz (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 9 ha are registered under vine.
de-ober-ingelheim-pares.nerd_note: Charlemagne built a palace at Ingelheim; legend says that from here he saw the snow melt first on the slopes across the Rhine and ordered them planted with vines.

de-oberdiebach-furstenberg.name: Oberdiebacher Fürstenberg
de-oberdiebach-furstenberg.summary: A steep Oberdiebach site of about 21 ha below the Fürstenberg castle ruin, giving fine, aromatic Riesling.
de-oberdiebach-furstenberg.terroir: Slate on a steep slope in the Diebach valley. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Loreley and the Grosslage Schloß Stahleck (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 21.2 ha are registered under vine.

de-oberemmel-agritiusberg.name: Oberemmeler Agritiusberg
de-oberemmel-agritiusberg.summary: A small Oberemmel site named after St. Agritius, a fourth-century bishop of Trier, once more highly regarded than it is today.
de-oberemmel-agritiusberg.terroir: Slate on the Oberemmel side valley. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 2.7 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Oberemmel include Rosenberg and Hütte.

de-oberemmel-hutte.name: Oberemmeler Hütte
de-oberemmel-hutte.summary: The Hütte is the small, walled monopole of Weingut von Hövel in Oberemmel, a former property of St. Maximin abbey in Trier. It gives delicate, finely etched Riesling with a floral lift.
de-oberemmel-hutte.terroir: Steep slate on a south-facing side-valley slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Oberemmel include Rosenberg and Agritiusberg.

de-oberemmel-rosenberg.name: Oberemmeler Rosenberg
de-oberemmel-rosenberg.summary: Oberemmel's largest site (about 35 ha), the Rosenberg gives medium-bodied, floral Saar Riesling, notably from Reichsgraf von Kesselstatt.
de-oberemmel-rosenberg.terroir: Slate and loam in the Oberemmel valley, cooler than the main Saar. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 34.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Oberemmel include Agritiusberg and Hütte.

de-oberhausen-brucke.name: Oberhausener Brücke
de-oberhausen-brucke.summary: The Brücke is a tiny monopole of Dönnhoff next to the old bridge at Oberhausen, barely a hectare on the river bank. It is known for grippy, smoky Riesling and for Eiswein, because cold air settles over the water here on winter nights. It is one of the very few true monopoles of the Nahe.
de-oberhausen-brucke.terroir: Grey slate with loess and loam on a low, flat site right on the Nahe; the river both protects it in autumn and chills it in winter. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Burgweg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Oberhausen include Leistenberg.
de-oberhausen-brucke.nerd_note: Dönnhoff's Brücke Eisweins are among the most celebrated of the 1990s and 2000s.

de-oberhausen-leistenberg.name: Oberhausener Leistenberg
de-oberhausen-leistenberg.summary: A steep slate slope in Oberhausen of about 5 ha, where Dönnhoff makes a vibrant, fruity Riesling Kabinett.
de-oberhausen-leistenberg.terroir: Grey slate, south-facing, in a side valley. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Burgweg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 4.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Oberhausen include Brücke.

de-oberotterbach-sonnenberg.name: Sonnenberg
de-oberotterbach-sonnenberg.summary: The Sonnenberg runs across the French border at Schweigen: many of its vines lie in Alsace near Wissembourg but, under a long-standing cross-border arrangement, their grapes are made into German wine. Friedrich Becker and Bernhart make outstanding Pinot Noir here, with Becker's parcel wines (Kammerberg, Sankt Paul) among the best German reds. The best parcels lie on limestone ridges that continue south into Alsace.
de-oberotterbach-sonnenberg.terroir: About 276 ha registered, with limestone and marl in the best parcels and loess elsewhere. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Südl. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Guttenberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 276.4 ha are registered under vine.
de-oberotterbach-sonnenberg.nerd_note: Becker's Kammerberg parcel lies on French soil, which once forced the estate to label it without the site name.

de-oberwesel-bernstein.name: Oberweseler Bernstein
de-oberwesel-bernstein.summary: The Bernstein lies in the Engehöll side valley near Oberwesel, an old terraced site that Lanius-Knab bottles as Engehöller Bernstein: cool, perfumed Riesling with racy acidity.
de-oberwesel-bernstein.terroir: About 11 ha of slate on steep terraces. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Loreley and the Grosslage Schloß Schönburg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 10.6 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Oberwesel include Ölsberg.

de-oberwesel-olsberg.name: Oberweseler Ölsberg
de-oberwesel-olsberg.summary: The Ölsberg is a steep slope of slate on the right bank opposite Oberwesel, a small, terraced site giving dense, mineral Riesling.
de-oberwesel-olsberg.terroir: About 6 ha of slate terraces facing south-west across the Rhine. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Loreley and the Grosslage Schloß Schönburg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 5.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Oberwesel include Bernstein.

de-ockfen-bockstein.name: Ockfener Bockstein
de-ockfen-bockstein.summary: The Bockstein is Ockfen's great slope, about 52 ha of slate rising high above a side valley of the Saar. It is cooler and later-ripening than the Scharzhofberg, and its Rieslings are classically racy with grapefruit, herbs and a cool slate finish; in warm vintages it shines with fruity-sweet Kabinett and Spätlese. Sankt Urbans-Hof, Dr. Fischer, Zilliken and Van Volxem are among the owners.
de-ockfen-bockstein.terroir: Grey Devonian slate on a steep, south and south-west-facing slope from roughly 170 to 350 m, exposed to wind from the Hunsrück; the height of the slope keeps acidity high. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 51.7 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Ockfen include Geisberg.
de-ockfen-bockstein.nerd_note: Ockfen sits a little away from the Saar itself, so the Bockstein gets less of the river's warming effect than sites that rise straight out of the water.

de-ockfen-geisberg.name: Geisberg
de-ockfen-geisberg.summary: The Geisberg rises above Ockfen and Schoden to over 400 m, one of the highest sites on the Saar. Long abandoned, it has been cleared and replanted by Van Volxem, whose dry Geisberg Riesling is cool, perfumed and taut.
de-ockfen-geisberg.terroir: High, steep slate with a strong wind exposure; only a few hectares are under vine. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 3.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Ockfen include Bockstein.
de-ockfen-geisberg.nerd_note: Van Volxem's Roman Niewodniczanski replanted the Geisberg after studying the old Prussian maps and price lists that ranked Saar sites a century and more ago.

de-odernheim-kloster-disibodenberg.name: Odernheimer Kloster Disibodenberg
de-odernheim-kloster-disibodenberg.summary: This small site surrounds the ruins of the Disibodenberg monastery above Odernheim, where Hildegard of Bingen lived as a nun from 1112 until about 1150. Monks planted vines here in the Middle Ages, and today a single estate works about 7 ha.
de-odernheim-kloster-disibodenberg.terroir: South-facing slopes of red sandstone and volcanic soils around the abbey ruins at the meeting of the Nahe and Glan. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Paradiesgarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 7.1 ha are registered under vine.
de-odernheim-kloster-disibodenberg.nerd_note: Hildegard wrote about wine as medicine, and the Disibodenberg is one of the few places where you can stand in her vineyard.

de-oppenheim-sacktrager.name: Oppenheimer Sackträger
de-oppenheim-sacktrager.summary: The Sackträger ('sack carrier') is Oppenheim's best-known site, on limestone and loess above the old town, giving full, elegant Riesling and Silvaner.
de-oppenheim-sacktrager.terroir: About 19 ha of limestone, marl and loess, facing south-east. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nierstein and the Grosslage Güldenmorgen (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 19.3 ha are registered under vine.
de-oppenheim-sacktrager.nerd_note: Oppenheim's medieval cellars form a labyrinth of passages under the town, now partly open to visitors.

de-piesport-domherr.name: Piesporter Domherr
de-piesport-domherr.summary: The Domherr ('cathedral canon') is a small, steep heart of the Piesport amphitheatre, historically owned by the Trier cathedral chapter. Its Riesling is concentrated and finely spiced.
de-piesport-domherr.terroir: About 4 ha of slate in the steepest part of the bowl. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Michelsberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 4.2 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Piesport include Schubertslay.

de-piesport-schubertslay.name: Piesporter Schubertslay
de-piesport-schubertslay.summary: A tiny, very steep rock face in Piesport that Julian Haart and a few others have revived, giving intense, stony Riesling.
de-piesport-schubertslay.terroir: Bare slate cliff facing south. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Michelsberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Piesport include Domherr.

de-punderich-marienburg.name: Pündericher Marienburg
de-punderich-marienburg.summary: The Marienburg rises opposite Pünderich below a ruined convent, a long, steep wall of slate that Clemens Busch has divided into parcels by rock type: blue slate in the Fahrlay, grey in the Falkenlay, red in the Rothenpfad and the old Raffes terraces. Each gives a different organic Riesling, from cool and mineral to warm and spicy, a lesson in how slate colour changes wine.
de-punderich-marienburg.terroir: About 50 ha of grey, blue and red Devonian slate on very steep south to south-west slopes, many still terraced with dry-stone walls. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Vom heißen Stein (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 50.2 ha are registered under vine.
de-punderich-marienburg.nerd_note: Busch's parcel bottlings revived historic names that the 1971 law had merged into the single Marienburg.

de-rech-herrenberg.name: Recher Herrenberg
de-rech-herrenberg.summary: A Rech site of about 18 ha on slate, giving fine Pinot Noir and some Riesling, close to the old stone bridge of Rech.
de-rech-herrenberg.terroir: Slate and greywacke slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Walporzheim/Ahrtal and the Grosslage Klosterberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 17.8 ha are registered under vine.

de-rummelsheim-schlossberg.name: Rümmelsheimer Schloßberg
de-rummelsheim-schlossberg.summary: The slope below the castle of Burg Layen in Rümmelsheim, home of Schlossgut Diel, giving fine, mineral Riesling that Diel sells as Burg Layener Schlossberg.
de-rummelsheim-schlossberg.terroir: About 15 ha of quartzite and slate on south-facing slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Schlosskapelle (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 15 ha are registered under vine.

de-ruppertsberg-gaisbohl.name: Ruppertsberger Gaisböhl
de-ruppertsberg-gaisbohl.summary: The Gaisböhl is a walled monopole of Dr. Bürklin-Wolf in Ruppertsberg, giving a firm, citrus-driven Riesling that Bürklin-Wolf ranks as a grand cru.
de-ruppertsberg-gaisbohl.terroir: Sandy loam with sandstone and some basalt. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Hofstück (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Ruppertsberg include Reiterpfad, Hoheburg and Spiess.

de-ruppertsberg-hoheburg.name: Ruppertsberger Hoheburg
de-ruppertsberg-hoheburg.summary: A Ruppertsberg site of about 18 ha giving fruity, approachable Riesling, notably from Bürklin-Wolf.
de-ruppertsberg-hoheburg.terroir: Sandy loam over gravel. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Hofstück (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 18.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Ruppertsberg include Reiterpfad, Gaisböhl and Spiess.

de-ruppertsberg-reiterpfad.name: Ruppertsberger Reiterpfad
de-ruppertsberg-reiterpfad.summary: A large Ruppertsberg site of about 77 ha whose best parcels give rich, aromatic Riesling, notably from von Buhl, Christmann and Bassermann-Jordan.
de-ruppertsberg-reiterpfad.terroir: Sand, loam and limestone. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Hofstück (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 77.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Ruppertsberg include Hoheburg, Gaisböhl and Spiess.

de-ruppertsberg-spiess.name: Ruppertsberger Spiess
de-ruppertsberg-spiess.summary: A small Ruppertsberg site of about 5.5 ha giving fine, mineral Riesling, from von Buhl and Bürklin-Wolf.
de-ruppertsberg-spiess.terroir: Sandy loam and sandstone. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Hofstück (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 5.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Ruppertsberg include Reiterpfad, Hoheburg and Gaisböhl.

de-saarburg-kupp.name: Saarburger Kupp
de-saarburg-kupp.summary: A Saarburg slope above the town, the Kupp gives light, floral Riesling for several local estates.
de-saarburg-kupp.terroir: Slate on a south-east-facing hill. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 10.6 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Saarburg include Rausch.

de-saarburg-rausch.name: Saarburger Rausch
de-saarburg-rausch.summary: The Saarburger Rausch is the signature site of Forstmeister Geltz Zilliken, a steep slope of slate above Saarburg laced with a volcanic diabase intrusion. Zilliken's fruity-sweet Kabinett, Spätlese and Auslese from the Rausch are some of the most age-worthy wines of the Mosel, with a smoky, spicy note and a nervy acidity that keeps them fresh for decades. The estate's cellar, dug three storeys deep, keeps temperatures low and fermentations slow.
de-saarburg-rausch.terroir: Around 18 ha of grey slate mixed with greenish diabase (greenstone), south-facing at roughly 200 to 300 m; the hard diabase holds less water and stresses the vines. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 18.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Saarburg include Kupp.
de-saarburg-rausch.nerd_note: The diabase gives the Rausch a smoky, spicy signature that tasters pick out even in very young wines.

de-schlossbockelheim-felsenberg.name: Schloßböckelheimer Felsenberg
de-schlossbockelheim-felsenberg.summary: The Felsenberg ('rock hill') is a steep, rocky slope at Schlossböckelheim, the source of some of the Nahe's most precise dry Rieslings from Dönnhoff and Schäfer-Fröhlich. The wines are cool, smoky and intensely mineral, with herbal notes from the volcanic soils. The village takes its name from Böckelheim castle, where Emperor Henry IV was imprisoned by his own son in 1105; the castle ruins still crown the hill.
de-schlossbockelheim-felsenberg.terroir: About 10.6 ha of weathered rhyolite (porphyry) with little soil, on steep south-facing slopes above the Nahe. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Burgweg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 10.6 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Schloßböckelheim include In den Felsen and Kupfergrube.

de-schlossbockelheim-in-den-felsen.name: Schloßböckelheimer In den Felsen
de-schlossbockelheim-in-den-felsen.summary: A small Schlossböckelheim site of about 6.5 ha among rock outcrops, giving fine, stony Riesling.
de-schlossbockelheim-in-den-felsen.terroir: Porphyry rock with thin soils. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Burgweg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 6.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Schloßböckelheim include Felsenberg and Kupfergrube.

de-schlossbockelheim-kupfergrube.name: Schloßböckelheimer Kupfergrube
de-schlossbockelheim-kupfergrube.summary: The Kupfergrube ('copper mine') takes its name from old copper workings in the hillside. Early in the twentieth century the Prussian state domain cleared and terraced it, and it quickly became one of the Nahe's grand sites. Schäfer-Fröhlich and Gut Hermannsberg make tense, smoky, spicy Riesling here.
de-schlossbockelheim-kupfergrube.terroir: About 12.6 ha of volcanic rock (melaphyre and rhyolite) on steep terraces facing south. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Burgweg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 12.6 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Schloßböckelheim include Felsenberg and In den Felsen.
de-schlossbockelheim-kupfergrube.nerd_note: Before it was planted the hill was covered with scrub; the domain proved that a site with no vineyard history could become a grand cru in one generation.

de-schoden-saarfeilser-marienberg.name: Schodener Saarfeilser Marienberg
de-schoden-saarfeilser-marienberg.summary: A tiny Schoden site with a historic double name, giving taut, cool Saar Riesling.
de-schoden-saarfeilser-marienberg.terroir: Steep slate on the Saar's left bank. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 3.4 ha are registered under vine.

de-serrig-herrenberg.name: Serriger Herrenberg
de-serrig-herrenberg.summary: Serrig's Herrenberg is a cool, late-ripening slope that gives tart, stony Riesling in lean years and thrilling ones in warm vintages. Serrig was a centre of Prussian state viticulture.
de-serrig-herrenberg.terroir: Slate on steep south-west slopes near the upper limit of the Saar vineyards. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Serrig include Schloß Saarfelser Schloßberg, Schloß Saarsteiner and Würtzberg.

de-serrig-schloss-saarfelser-schlossberg.name: Serriger Schloß Saarfelser Schloßberg
de-serrig-schloss-saarfelser-schlossberg.summary: A Serrig site named after the Saarfels castle-estate, giving cool, crisp Riesling from steep slate.
de-serrig-schloss-saarfelser-schlossberg.terroir: Slate slopes on the upstream Saar. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Serrig include Herrenberg, Schloß Saarsteiner and Würtzberg.

de-serrig-schloss-saarsteiner.name: Serriger Schloß Saarsteiner
de-serrig-schloss-saarsteiner.summary: The monopole of Schloss Saarstein, a villa-estate high above the Saar near Serrig, this is one of the coolest sites of the valley. The Ebert family makes bright, piercing Riesling and elegant Pinot Blanc here.
de-serrig-schloss-saarsteiner.terroir: Steep slate on a south-facing bend of the river, among the most upstream top sites of the Saar. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Serrig include Herrenberg, Schloß Saarfelser Schloßberg and Würtzberg.

de-serrig-wurtzberg.name: Serriger Würtzberg
de-serrig-wurtzberg.summary: The Würtzberg in Serrig, about 5.5 ha registered, gives lean, aromatic Riesling and lent its name to an estate founded on Prussian-era vineyards.
de-serrig-wurtzberg.terroir: Steep slate on the Saar's cool upper reaches. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 5.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Serrig include Herrenberg, Schloß Saarfelser Schloßberg and Schloß Saarsteiner.

de-siebeldingen-im-sonnenschein.name: Siebeldingener Im Sonnenschein
de-siebeldingen-im-sonnenschein.summary: Im Sonnenschein ('in the sunshine') at Siebeldingen is the flagship of Ökonomierat Rebholz, whose dry Riesling, Pinot Blanc and Pinot Noir from here are taut and long-lived.
de-siebeldingen-im-sonnenschein.terroir: About 97 ha registered, shell limestone and loam on south-facing slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Südl. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Königsgarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 97.1 ha are registered under vine.

de-siefersheim-goldenes-horn.name: Siefersheimer Goldenes Horn
de-siefersheim-goldenes-horn.summary: A Siefersheim site of about 75 ha on volcanic and sandy soils, giving fresh, fruity white wines.
de-siefersheim-goldenes-horn.terroir: Porphyry and sand in the western hills. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bingen and the Grosslage Rheingrafenstein (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 74.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Siefersheim include Höllberg.

de-siefersheim-hollberg.name: Siefersheimer Höllberg
de-siefersheim-hollberg.summary: The Höllberg at Siefersheim is a high, rocky site of volcanic porphyry in the 'Rheinhessian Switzerland', the hilly west of the region. Wagner-Stempel makes a cool, smoky, very mineral Riesling here. The name is usually read as 'hell hill', after the heat that builds up on its rocks.
de-siefersheim-hollberg.terroir: About 29 ha of rhyolite (porphyry) rubble on a south-facing slope at up to about 300 m. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bingen and the Grosslage Rheingrafenstein (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 28.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Siefersheim include Goldenes Horn.
de-siefersheim-hollberg.nerd_note: Porphyry links Siefersheim geologically to the neighbouring Nahe rather than to the limestone of the Wonnegau.

de-thornich-ritsch.name: Thörnicher Ritsch
de-thornich-ritsch.summary: The Ritsch is a steep slope above Thörnich that Carl Loewen helped rescue from abandonment. Its Riesling is cool, smoky and tightly wound.
de-thornich-ritsch.terroir: About 15 ha of slate on a south-west-facing slope at a narrow part of the valley. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Sankt Michael (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 15.1 ha are registered under vine.

de-traisen-bastei.name: Traisener Bastei
de-traisen-bastei.summary: The Bastei is a narrow strip of vines at the foot of the Rotenfels, the tallest rock face between the Alps and Scandinavia, about 200 m of red rhyolite. Only about 1.7 ha are planted, on scree that has fallen from the cliff; Dr. Crusius makes an intense, smoky, almost spicy Riesling from it, among the warmest sites of the Nahe.
de-traisen-bastei.terroir: Rhyolite scree at the base of a south-facing cliff that stores and radiates heat onto the vines. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Burgweg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 1.7 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Traisen include Rotenfels.
de-traisen-bastei.nerd_note: Climbers and hikers on the Rotenfels look straight down onto the Bastei; the cliff is a nature reserve.

de-traisen-rotenfels.name: Traisener Rotenfels
de-traisen-rotenfels.summary: A Traisen site of about 16 ha below and beside the Rotenfels cliff, giving ripe, spicy Riesling, notably from Dr. Crusius.
de-traisen-rotenfels.terroir: Red rhyolite and weathered volcanic soils. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Burgweg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 15.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Traisen include Bastei.

de-trarbach-huhnerberg.name: Trarbacher Hühnerberg
de-trarbach-huhnerberg.summary: A small, steep side-valley site in Trarbach, giving intense, cool Riesling, notably from Martin Müllen.
de-trarbach-huhnerberg.terroir: Slate in the Kautenbach valley, cooler than the main river. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Schwarzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 2.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Trarbach include Ungsberg.

de-trarbach-ungsberg.name: Trarbacher Ungsberg
de-trarbach-ungsberg.summary: A tiny Trarbach site of under 2 ha, giving fine, fragrant Riesling from a handful of growers.
de-trarbach-ungsberg.terroir: Steep slate above Trarbach. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Schwarzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 1.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Trarbach include Hühnerberg.

de-trittenheim-altarchen.name: Trittenheimer Altärchen
de-trittenheim-altarchen.summary: Trittenheim's big Altärchen (about 155 ha) wraps around the village side of the river bend and is a source of honest, fruity Riesling, with a few steep parcels capable of much more.
de-trittenheim-altarchen.terroir: Slate and weathered loam, from steep to gentle. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Michelsberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 154.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Trittenheim include Apotheke, Felsenkopf and Leiterchen.

de-trittenheim-apotheke.name: Trittenheimer Apotheke
de-trittenheim-apotheke.summary: The Apotheke is a long, steep wall of slate across the river from Trittenheim, about 65 ha that run around a bend of the Mosel. Grans-Fassian, Ansgar Clüsserath and Josef Milz are its best-known growers, and it produces some of the most finely balanced dry Rieslings of the Middle Mosel: peach and citrus, a smoky slate edge and a lively finish. Old ungrafted vines survive in several parcels.
de-trittenheim-apotheke.terroir: Grey and blue Devonian slate on slopes up to 70 percent, mostly south-west facing, from the river at about 120 m up to roughly 300 m; the broad water surface reflects light and tempers frost. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Michelsberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 65.1 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Trittenheim include Altärchen, Felsenkopf and Leiterchen.
de-trittenheim-apotheke.nerd_note: Workers once had to cross the river by ferry to reach the slope; the modern bridge only came in the twentieth century.

de-trittenheim-felsenkopf.name: Trittenheimer Felsenkopf
de-trittenheim-felsenkopf.summary: The Felsenkopf ('rock head') is a tiny, very steep outcrop above Trittenheim owned by Josef Milz, who makes a concentrated, mineral Riesling here. It is classified as a VDP.GROSSE LAGE.
de-trittenheim-felsenkopf.terroir: Bare slate rock with almost no topsoil. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Michelsberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Trittenheim include Altärchen, Apotheke and Leiterchen.

de-trittenheim-leiterchen.name: Trittenheimer Leiterchen
de-trittenheim-leiterchen.summary: The Leiterchen ('little ladder') is a narrow strip of steep slate in Trittenheim, a monopole of Josef Milz. Its Riesling is fine and floral, and the site is a VDP.GROSSE LAGE.
de-trittenheim-leiterchen.terroir: Steep slate so narrow that workers once climbed it by ladder. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Michelsberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Trittenheim include Altärchen, Apotheke and Felsenkopf.

de-ungstein-herrenberg.name: Ungsteiner Herrenberg
de-ungstein-herrenberg.summary: A Ungstein site of about 29 ha giving juicy, aromatic Riesling, from Pfeffingen and others.
de-ungstein-herrenberg.terroir: Limestone and loam. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Honigsäckel (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 28.6 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Ungstein include Weilberg.

de-ungstein-weilberg.name: Ungsteiner Weilberg
de-ungstein-weilberg.summary: The Weilberg at Ungstein is named after a Roman villa (villa rustica) excavated in the vineyard, complete with a Roman wine press. It gives spicy, intense Riesling on limestone and red soils, notably from Pfeffingen and Rings. The excavated Roman estate, with its wine-pressing basins, is open to visitors among the vines and shows that grapes were pressed here about 1,700 years ago.
de-ungstein-weilberg.terroir: About 33 ha of limestone with red, iron-rich clay (terra rossa) on a south-east slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Honigsäckel (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 32.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Ungstein include Herrenberg.

de-urzig-wurzgarten.name: Ürziger Würzgarten
de-urzig-wurzgarten.summary: The Würzgarten ('spice garden') is a dramatic slope of red soil and slate cliffs above Ürzig, unlike anything else on the Mosel. Its Rieslings have a uniquely exotic spice, red fruits and a savoury, almost earthy depth. Many vines are ungrafted and very old, because phylloxera struggled in these soils. Dr. Loosen, Mönchhof, Jos. Christoffel, Rebenhof and Markus Molitor are key growers, and a tiny sundial parcel sits in the middle of the cliff.
de-urzig-wurzgarten.terroir: About 51 ha where red Rotliegend sandstone and volcanic material overlie Devonian slate, giving red, iron-rich soils; the slope is terraced in places, south-facing and extremely steep, with walls and rock outcrops that store heat. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Schwarzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 50.9 ha are registered under vine.
de-urzig-wurzgarten.nerd_note: The red soils are a remnant of the Wittlich basin's Permian deposits, which reach the Mosel only at Ürzig and Erden.

de-valwig-herrenberg.name: Valwiger Herrenberg
de-valwig-herrenberg.summary: A steep Valwig slope of about 18 ha in a loop of the river near Cochem, giving spicy, rich Riesling.
de-valwig-herrenberg.terroir: Terraced slate on a south-facing bend. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Burg Cochem and the Grosslage Rosenhang (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 17.9 ha are registered under vine.

de-wachenheim-belz.name: Wachenheimer Belz
de-wachenheim-belz.summary: A small Wachenheim site at the forest edge, giving cool, elegant Riesling.
de-wachenheim-belz.terroir: Sandstone and loam on a higher slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Wachenheim include Böhlig, Gerümpel, Goldbächel and Rechbächel.

de-wachenheim-bohlig.name: Wachenheimer Böhlig
de-wachenheim-bohlig.summary: A Wachenheim site of about 5.5 ha giving firm, spicy Riesling, for example from Bürklin-Wolf.
de-wachenheim-bohlig.terroir: Sandstone, loam and limestone. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 5.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Wachenheim include Gerümpel, Goldbächel, Belz and Rechbächel.

de-wachenheim-gerumpel.name: Wachenheimer Gerümpel
de-wachenheim-gerumpel.summary: The Gerümpel is Wachenheim's most famous site, giving vibrant, precise Riesling from Bürklin-Wolf, Karl Schaefer and others.
de-wachenheim-gerumpel.terroir: About 13 ha of sandstone, sand and loam on a gentle east-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 12.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Wachenheim include Böhlig, Goldbächel, Belz and Rechbächel.

de-wachenheim-goldbachel.name: Wachenheimer Goldbächel
de-wachenheim-goldbachel.summary: A small Wachenheim site of about 4 ha giving lively, mineral Riesling.
de-wachenheim-goldbachel.terroir: Sandstone and loam. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Wachenheim include Böhlig, Gerümpel, Belz and Rechbächel.

de-wachenheim-rechbachel.name: Wachenheimer Rechbächel
de-wachenheim-rechbachel.summary: A small walled Wachenheim site, a monopole of Bürklin-Wolf, giving fine, fragrant Riesling.
de-wachenheim-rechbachel.terroir: Sandstone and loam behind walls. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Wachenheim include Böhlig, Gerümpel, Goldbächel and Belz.

de-wallhausen-johannisberg.name: Wallhausener Johannisberg
de-wallhausen-johannisberg.summary: The Johannisberg at Wallhausen is a home site of Prinz Salm, an estate whose family has made wine here for centuries and claims one of Germany's longest unbroken wine-growing lineages. It gives fine, floral Riesling on mixed soils.
de-wallhausen-johannisberg.terroir: About 11 ha of slate, quartzite and loam in the Gräfenbach valley. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Pfarrgarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 10.8 ha are registered under vine.

de-wawern-goldberg.name: Wawerner Goldberg
de-wawern-goldberg.summary: The Wawerner Goldberg is a south-facing amphitheatre in a little side valley of the Saar that had fallen out of use before Van Volxem bought and replanted it. The site is now a VDP.GROSSE LAGE and gives full, golden-fruited dry Riesling with Saar spine.
de-wawern-goldberg.terroir: About 12 ha of slate in a warm, wind-protected bowl. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 12 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Wawern include Herrenberger.

de-wawern-herrenberger.name: Wawerner Herrenberger
de-wawern-herrenberger.summary: A small Wawern site with a long reputation for fine, fragrant Riesling, bottled by a few estates including Dr. Fischer.
de-wawern-herrenberger.terroir: Slate on a steep south-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 3.6 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Wawern include Goldberg.

de-wehlen-klosterberg.name: Wehlener Klosterberg
de-wehlen-klosterberg.summary: A Wehlen site of about 14 ha behind the village, giving fresh, fruity Riesling.
de-wehlen-klosterberg.terroir: Slate and loam, moderately steep. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Münzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 14.3 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Wehlen include Sonnenuhr and Nonnenberg.

de-wehlen-nonnenberg.name: Wehlener Nonnenberg
de-wehlen-nonnenberg.summary: A small Wehlen site of about 2.4 ha on the village side of the river, once owned by a convent, giving lighter Riesling.
de-wehlen-nonnenberg.terroir: Gentler slopes of slate and loam. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Münzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 2.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Wehlen include Sonnenuhr and Klosterberg.

de-wehlen-sonnenuhr.name: Wehlener Sonnenuhr
de-wehlen-sonnenuhr.summary: The Wehlener Sonnenuhr is the archetype of fruity-sweet Mosel Riesling: a steep, south-facing slope across the river from Wehlen, marked by a sundial that Jodocus Prüm built in 1842 so workers could tell the time. Joh. Jos. Prüm's Kabinett, Spätlese and Auslese from here are among the most collected white wines on earth, famous for their feather-light body, mineral spritz and capacity to age half a century. Dr. Loosen, S.A. Prüm, Selbach-Oster, Markus Molitor and Wegeler also own parcels.
de-wehlen-sonnenuhr.terroir: About 43 ha of grey Devonian slate on slopes of up to 60 percent, facing south to south-west over a broad stretch of river, which reflects light and stores warmth; the slate warms the shallow soils and helps ripen grapes late into autumn. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Münzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 42.6 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Wehlen include Klosterberg and Nonnenberg.
de-wehlen-sonnenuhr.nerd_note: J.J. Prüm's wines are famous for a reductive, sulphury note when young, often mistaken for a fault; it fades with a few years in bottle.

de-westhofen-aulerde.name: Westhofener Aulerde
de-westhofen-aulerde.summary: The Aulerde lies on lower, warmer ground in Westhofen with sandy loam and gravel, giving generous, juicy Riesling from Wittmann and Gutzler.
de-westhofen-aulerde.terroir: About 100 ha of loam, sand and gravel. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Wonnegau and the Grosslage Bergkloster (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 102.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Westhofen include Morstein, Steingrube, Kirchspiel and Brunnenhäuschen.

de-westhofen-brunnenhauschen.name: Westhofener Brunnenhäuschen
de-westhofen-brunnenhauschen.summary: The Brunnenhäuschen ('little well house') sits high above Westhofen on red-tinged limestone soils. Keller's Abtserde, one of Germany's most coveted Rieslings, comes from a parcel inside it; Wittmann also bottles a Grosses Gewächs. It is the highest of the Westhofen grand sites, and its wines tend to be the most tightly wound when young.
de-westhofen-brunnenhauschen.terroir: About 31 ha of terra rossa-like reddish clay over limestone, the highest part of Westhofen. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Wonnegau and the Grosslage Bergkloster (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 31.1 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Westhofen include Morstein, Steingrube, Aulerde and Kirchspiel.
de-westhofen-brunnenhauschen.nerd_note: Abtserde ('abbot's earth') recalls medieval monastic ownership of the parcel.

de-westhofen-kirchspiel.name: Westhofener Kirchspiel
de-westhofen-kirchspiel.summary: The Kirchspiel is a Westhofen amphitheatre facing south-east towards the village church, giving finely fruited, elegant dry Riesling from Wittmann, Keller and Groebe. Kirchspiel means 'parish', a reminder of church ownership. Wittmann farms biodynamically, and his Kirchspiel Grosses Gewächs is often the most elegant of his three Westhofen grand sites: the amphitheatre concentrates warmth while the limestone keeps the wine tight.
de-westhofen-kirchspiel.terroir: About 44 ha of limestone and marl in a sheltered bowl. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Wonnegau and the Grosslage Bergkloster (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 43.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Westhofen include Morstein, Steingrube, Aulerde and Brunnenhäuschen.

de-westhofen-morstein.name: Westhofener Morstein
de-westhofen-morstein.summary: The Morstein is the jewel of Westhofen and one of the great Rieslings sites of Germany, a gentle south-facing slope on the edge of the Wonnegau hills. Philipp Wittmann and Klaus Peter Keller make powerful, chiselled dry Rieslings here, with yellow fruit, herbs and a long chalky finish; they age for decades. Gutzler and Groebe are also important.
de-westhofen-morstein.terroir: Clay marl over fissured limestone, with deep roots reaching water even in dry summers; the slope is open to the south and fairly high for Rheinhessen, which keeps acidity firm. About 150 ha are registered in the wider Einzellage, though the classic core is much smaller. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Wonnegau and the Grosslage Bergkloster (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 152.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Westhofen include Steingrube, Aulerde, Kirchspiel and Brunnenhäuschen.
de-westhofen-morstein.nerd_note: Before the 1990s Westhofen was known for bulk wine; the Morstein became a symbol of the Rheinhessen revolution led by young growers.

de-westhofen-steingrube.name: Westhofener Steingrube
de-westhofen-steingrube.summary: A large Westhofen site of about 144 ha on limestone, giving fresh white and red wines, with Pinot Noir from some growers.
de-westhofen-steingrube.terroir: Limestone and marl on gentle slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Wonnegau and the Grosslage Bergkloster (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 144 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Westhofen include Morstein, Aulerde, Kirchspiel and Brunnenhäuschen.

de-wiltingen-braune-kupp.name: Wiltingener Braune Kupp
de-wiltingen-braune-kupp.summary: A small, steep amphitheatre of brown-weathering slate just upstream of Wiltingen, the Braune Kupp is the monopole of Weingut Le Gallais, which Egon Müller's family has run since 1954. The wines are a shade broader and spicier than the neighbouring Scharzhofberg, with ripe yellow fruit, a smoky note and the same razor-sharp Saar acidity. Müller bottles them separately under the Le Gallais label, mostly as fruity-sweet Kabinett, Spätlese and Auslese that age as long as their more famous siblings.
de-wiltingen-braune-kupp.terroir: Iron-tinged Devonian slate on a south-facing curve that traps warmth; the bowl shape gives it a slightly earlier ripening rhythm than the open Scharzhofberg. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Wiltingen include Klosterberg, Braunfels, Kupp and Gottesfuß.
de-wiltingen-braune-kupp.nerd_note: The name means 'brown dome', after the colour of the weathered rock rather than any wine style.

de-wiltingen-braunfels.name: Wiltingener Braunfels
de-wiltingen-braunfels.summary: A larger Wiltingen site (about 20 ha) on the road towards Kanzem, Braunfels is a source of elegant, mid-weight Saar Riesling from growers such as Van Volxem and Jordan & Jordan. It sits a step below the village's grand sites but shows the same slate-driven tension.
de-wiltingen-braunfels.terroir: Slate with more weathered loam on gentler pitches; ripens a little later than the steep core of Wiltingen. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 20.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Wiltingen include Klosterberg, Braune Kupp, Kupp and Gottesfuß.

de-wiltingen-gottesfuss.name: Wiltingener Gottesfuß
de-wiltingen-gottesfuss.summary: Gottesfuß ('God's foot') is a tiny, very steep slope at the edge of Wiltingen that Van Volxem has made famous with ungrafted vines planted more than a century ago. The site gives dense, chiselled dry Riesling with a herbal, almost saline finish and the concentration that only old, low-yielding vines provide. Around 3.5 ha are registered under vine.
de-wiltingen-gottesfuss.terroir: Grey and blue Devonian slate with little topsoil on a sheltered south-facing flank; the old own-rooted vines dig deep into the fissured rock. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 3.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Wiltingen include Klosterberg, Braunfels, Braune Kupp and Kupp.
de-wiltingen-gottesfuss.nerd_note: Phylloxera never took hold in much of the Saar's slate, which is why parcels like this still carry pre-1900 ungrafted vines.

de-wiltingen-holle.name: Wiltingener Hölle
de-wiltingen-holle.summary: Hölle ('hell') is a very small, hot pocket of steep slate in Wiltingen whose name reflects the heat that builds up in summer. It yields concentrated, ripe Saar Riesling from a handful of growers.
de-wiltingen-holle.terroir: South-facing slate bowl, sheltered from wind. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Wiltingen include Klosterberg, Braunfels, Braune Kupp and Kupp.

de-wiltingen-klosterberg.name: Wiltingener Klosterberg
de-wiltingen-klosterberg.summary: Wiltingen's largest Einzellage (about 50 ha), the Klosterberg spreads over the hills behind the village. It gives fresh, slatey Riesling of varying ambition; the best parcels show that much of the old Saar fame lay in small named plots that the 1971 law folded into larger Einzellagen.
de-wiltingen-klosterberg.terroir: Mixed grey slate and loam, from steep to rolling; quality depends heavily on the parcel. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 49.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Wiltingen include Braunfels, Braune Kupp, Kupp and Gottesfuß.

de-wiltingen-kupp.name: Wiltingener Kupp
de-wiltingen-kupp.summary: The Wiltinger Kupp is a compact, south-east-facing hill above the village, worked mainly by Van Volxem and the Bischöfliche Weingüter. Its Rieslings are firm and mineral with a cooler, more citric profile than the Braune Kupp next door.
de-wiltingen-kupp.terroir: Grey slate on a convex slope that catches morning sun and the cooling Saar breeze. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 7 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Wiltingen include Klosterberg, Braunfels, Braune Kupp and Gottesfuß.
