de-wiltingen-scharzhofberg.name: Scharzhofberg
de-wiltingen-scharzhofberg.summary: The Scharzhofberg is the Saar's crown and, for many, the purest expression of German Riesling anywhere. A single south-facing whale-back of grey Devonian slate rising above the Scharzhof manor between Wiltingen and Oberemmel, it gives wines of glassy acidity, almost weightless body and a perfume of white peach, citrus peel and wet stone that can take decades to unfold. Egon Müller's sweet Kabinett, Spätlese and Auslese set the benchmark, and his Trockenbeerenauslesen are among the most expensive wines ever auctioned: a 2003 TBA fetched 14,566 euros a bottle at the VDP Mosel auction in 2015. Van Volxem, Reichsgraf von Kesselstatt, Vereinigte Hospitien and the Bischöfliche Weingüter also own parcels.
de-wiltingen-scharzhofberg.terroir: About 28 ha of vines on a steep, open slope from the valley floor to the wooded crest. Thin, stony grey slate warms quickly, but the Saar valley is cooler and windier than the Middle Mosel, so ripening is slow and late: in lean years the wines are taut, in warm years they gain an incomparable tension between ripeness and acidity.
de-wiltingen-scharzhofberg.nerd_note: Legally the Scharzhofberg is an Ortsteil (a named part of Wiltingen), which is why its wines carry no village prefix and why the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register files its 28 ha as 'Einzellagenfrei'. On Clotten's 1868 Prussian tax map it is shaded dark red, the top class.

de-winningen-bruckstuck.name: Winningener Brückstück
de-winningen-bruckstuck.summary: A Winningen site of about 8 ha by the old bridge, giving lively, mineral Riesling, for example from Knebel.
de-winningen-bruckstuck.terroir: Terraced slate on the lower Mosel. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Burg Cochem and the Grosslage Weinhex (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Winningen include Hamm.

de-winningen-hamm.name: Winningener Hamm
de-winningen-hamm.summary: A steep Winningen slope of about 11.5 ha, giving firm, fruity Riesling.
de-winningen-hamm.terroir: Slate terraces above the village. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Burg Cochem and the Grosslage Weinhex (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 11.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Winningen include Brückstück.

de-wintrich-grosser-herrgott.name: Wintricher Großer Herrgott
de-wintrich-grosser-herrgott.summary: A large Wintrich site of about 90 ha named after a wayside crucifix, giving fruity, accessible Riesling.
de-wintrich-grosser-herrgott.terroir: Slate and loam on moderate slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Kurfürstlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 90.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Wintrich include Ohligsberg.

de-wintrich-ohligsberg.name: Wintricher Ohligsberg
de-wintrich-ohligsberg.summary: The Ohligsberg is a very steep, rock-strewn slope above Wintrich, owned almost entirely by Reinhold Haart. Its Riesling is dense and mineral, with a distinctive smoky, almost flinty character. The slope is so stony that machines are useless here; vines are trained on single stakes (Einzelpfahl), the traditional Mosel system, and every task is done by hand.
de-wintrich-ohligsberg.terroir: About 7 ha of bare blue and grey slate, among the steepest sites of the Middle Mosel. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Kurfürstlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 6.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Wintrich include Großer Herrgott.
de-wintrich-ohligsberg.nerd_note: In the nineteenth century the Ohligsberg's wines were sold at prices to rival the best of Piesport.

de-wolf-goldgrube.name: Wolfer Goldgrube
de-wolf-goldgrube.summary: The Goldgrube in Wolf was all but forgotten until the Swiss grower Daniel Vollenweider started reviving its terraces in 2000. Today it gives finely spiced, mineral Riesling, dry and sweet.
de-wolf-goldgrube.terroir: About 7 ha of steep slate terraces above Traben-Trarbach. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Schwarzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 7 ha are registered under vine.

de-worms-liebfrauenstift-kirchenstuck.name: Wormser Liebfrauenstift-Kirchenstück
de-worms-liebfrauenstift-kirchenstuck.summary: This walled vineyard surrounds the Liebfrauenkirche in Worms, the church whose 'Liebfrauenmilch' gave its name to Germany's most famous and most debased wine style. Today a handful of estates make serious dry Riesling from the 12.5 ha around the church. The Gothic church rises out of the vines in the middle of the city, one of the very few urban grand sites in Germany.
de-worms-liebfrauenstift-kirchenstuck.terroir: Gravelly loam on the Rhine plain, sheltered by the church and town. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Wonnegau and the Grosslage Liebfrauenmorgen (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 12.5 ha are registered under vine.
de-worms-liebfrauenstift-kirchenstuck.nerd_note: In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries 'Liebfrauenmilch' meant the wine of this specific site; the name later spread to oceans of sweet blends.

de-zeltingen-rachtig-himmelreich.name: Zeltingen-Rachtiger Himmelreich
de-zeltingen-rachtig-himmelreich.summary: A large Zeltingen site of about 80 ha, giving fruity, gentle Riesling.
de-zeltingen-rachtig-himmelreich.terroir: Slate and loam on mixed slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Münzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 79.6 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Zeltingen-Rachtig include Schloßberg and Sonnenuhr.

de-zeltingen-rachtig-schlossberg.name: Zeltingen-Rachtiger Schloßberg
de-zeltingen-rachtig-schlossberg.summary: The Schlossberg rises behind Zeltingen around the site of a vanished castle. Selbach-Oster and Markus Molitor make powerful, spicy Riesling here, often dry.
de-zeltingen-rachtig-schlossberg.terroir: About 17 ha of slate with more weathered rock and a south-east exposure. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Münzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 16.7 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Zeltingen-Rachtig include Himmelreich and Sonnenuhr.

de-zeltingen-rachtig-sonnenuhr.name: Zeltingen-Rachtiger Sonnenuhr
de-zeltingen-rachtig-sonnenuhr.summary: Zeltingen's Sonnenuhr continues the Wehlener Sonnenuhr slope downstream and gives slightly broader, spicier wines. Selbach-Oster and Markus Molitor are the key growers, with old ungrafted vines. Zeltingen was long the largest wine village of the Middle Mosel. Selbach-Oster bottles its Rotlay parcel, ungrafted vines more than a century old, separately; the Sonnenuhr's wines are a touch broader than Wehlen's and age just as well.
de-zeltingen-rachtig-sonnenuhr.terroir: About 18.5 ha of grey slate, steep and south-facing. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Münzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 18.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Zeltingen-Rachtig include Himmelreich and Schloßberg.
